In the chain spec, no: it is not all-Codex globally.

Current routing is profile-driven per milestone:
- Current `sprint-00a` uses profile `nancy`.
- Several bakeoff-enabled milestones include `all-codex` as one arm, but the chain README says `chain start` records bakeoff metadata and does not auto-run bakeoffs.
- `sprint-07` is explicitly `profile: all-claude`, with the note saying that choice was deliberate because the thinking override is Claude-specific.
- Other milestones use `holmes`, `poirot`, `marlowe`, or `nancy`.

The live current plan status showed `plan` and `finalize` going through Hermes `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, and critique through Codex, which comes from the selected profile/config resolution rather than an all-Codex override. payload.get(\"tasks\") or payload.get(\"task_updates\") or []:\n+            if not isinstance(task, dict):\n+                continue\n+            for path in task.get(\"files_changed\") or []:\n+                if isinstance(path, str) and path.strip():\n+                    claimed_paths.add(path.strip())\n+\n+    repos: set[Path] = set()\n+    root_abs = root.resolve()\n+    for raw_path in claimed_paths:\n+        path = Path(raw_path)\n+        if path.is_absolute():\n+            try:\n+                path = path.resolve().relative_to(root_abs)\n+            except (OSError, ValueError):\n+                continue\n+        cursor = root\n+        for part in path.parts[:-1]:\n+            cursor = cursor / part\n+            if (cursor / \".git\").exists():\n+                repos.add(cursor)\n+                break\n+    return sorted(repos, key=lambda repo: repo.as_posix())\n+\n+\n+def _dirty_nested_repos_from_claimed_paths(root: Path, plan_name: str, *, writer) -> list[str]:\n+    dirty: list[str] = []\n+    root_abs = root.resolve()\n+    for repo in _claimed_nested_repos(root, plan_name):\n+        proc = subprocess.run(\n+            [\"git\", \"status\", \"--short\"],\n+            cwd=str(repo),\n+            capture_output=True,\n+            text=True,\n+            check=False,\n+            timeout=120,\n+        )\n+        writer(f\"[chain] git -C {repo} status --short -> rc={proc.returncode}\\n\")\n+        if proc.returncode != 0 or not proc.stdout.strip():\n+            continue\n+        try:\n+            rel = repo.resolve().relative_to(root_abs).as_posix()\n+        except (OSError, ValueError):\n+            rel = repo.as_posix()\n+        dirty.append(rel)\n+    return dirty\n+\n+\n def _commit_and_push_phase(root: Path, branch: str, plan: str, phase: str, *, writer) -> None:\n     \"\"\"Commit any current diff and push the milestone branch.\"\"\"\n+    dirty_nested = _dirty_nested_repos_from_claimed_paths(root, plan, writer=writer)\n+    if dirty_nested:\n+        raise CliError(\n+            \"nested_repo_changes_uncommitted\",\n+            \"Plan claimed changes in nested git repositories that top-level chain commits \"\n+            \"cannot publish: \"\n+            + \", \".join(dirty_nested)\n+            + \". Commit and push those nested repositories separately, or run the plan with \"\n+            \"a project_dir rooted at the repository being changed.\",\n+        )\n     _run_command(root, [\"git\", \"add\", \"-A\"], writer=writer, error_code=\"git_commit_failed\")\n*** End Patch\n"

This produced misleading associations for docs and gitlink markers that were not the real implementation work.\n+\n+Root cause location: execute quality path attribution.\n+\n+Partial harness fix made:\n+\n+- Nested-aware evidence validation reduces the false-negative path pressure that triggered attribution noise.\n+- Additional future work should further constrain auto-attribution so docs created by oversight/performance review are not assigned to unrelated sprint tasks unless explicitly claimed by the executor.\n+\n+### 4. `after_execute` Was Treated As Something The Executor Could Complete\n+\n+The finalized plan had an `after_execute` human action. The harness converted it into a synthetic executor task. That is brittle because a human handoff is not an implementation task; the executor can surface it, but cannot complete human sign-off.\n+\n+Root cause location: finalize handler.\n+\n+Harness fix made:\n+\n+- Stopped converting `after_execute` user actions into executor tasks.\n+- Added `user_actions.md` artifact generation so human actions are visible after finalize without blocking execution as fake work.\n+\n+### 5. Blocked Execute Could Not Recover\n+\n+After the quality gate blocked execution, `megaplan resume` could not run execute because the execute handler only allowed execution from `finalized`, not `blocked`.\n+\n+Root cause location: execute handler state guard.\n+\n+Harness fix made:\n+\n+- `handle_execute()` now accepts both `finalized` and `blocked` states, allowing execution recovery after a quality-gate block.\n+\n+### 6. Executor Output Overstated Human Completion\n+\n+The executor marked Section 12 checklist items as checked even though they still had placeholder owners such as `TBD-<engineering-lead>` and `TBD-<security-lead>`.\n+\n+Root cause location: execution/final review behavior, with a contributing spec ambiguity.\n+\n+The original intent said \"named owner.\" A placeholder is not a named owner. The executor treated \"surfaced for human assignment\" as enough to check the box. That interpretation is too loose for a kickoff gate.\n+\n+Fix made:\n+\n+- Corrected `docs/migration-vibecomfy.md` so owner-dependent rows remain unchecked until real owners are assigned.\n+- Updated the Sprint 0A performance review to distinguish \"executor complete\" from \"human gate complete.\"\n+\n+Future prompt/spec improvement:\n+\n+- For checklist gates, say explicitly: \"Do not check this row unless the owner field contains a real named person or explicitly approved role assignment. `TBD`, placeholder tokens, and generic functions are blockers.\"\n+\n+### 7. All-Codex Versus All-Claude Was Not Explicit Enough\n+\n+The chain was not globally all-Codex at the start. Sprint 0A used profile `nancy`. Some later bakeoff-enabled milestones included all-Codex arms, and the chain spec was modified during execution so Sprint 07 no longer used `all-claude`.\n+\n+Root cause location: chain spec/profile selection.\n+\n+Fix made:\n+\n+- The chain spec and README now more clearly record the intended profile strategy and the existence of performance reviews.\n+\n+Future improvement:\n+\n+- Add a preflight profile lint to Megaplan chains that reports all milestone profiles before execution starts.\n+- If the user asks \"all Codex,\" the chain should fail preflight if any milestone uses a Claude-only or mixed profile.\n+\n+## Harness Patches Made\n+\n+Patched in the live harness checkout at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan`:\n+\n+- `megaplan/evaluation.py`\n+- `megaplan/execute/quality.py`\n+- `megaplan/handlers/finalize.py`\n+- `megaplan/handlers/execute.py`\n+- `megaplan/chain.py`\n+- `tests/test_evaluation.py`\n+- `tests/test_finalize.py`\n+- `tests/test_execute.py`\n+- `tests/test_chain.py`\n+\n+Validation:\n+\n+```bash\n+PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m pytest tests/test_evaluation.py tests/test_finalize.py tests/test_chain.py tests/test_execute.py -q\n+```\n+\n+Result: 154 passed.\n+\n+## Product/Repo Changes Made\n+\n+In `reigh-app`:\n+\n+- `turbo_mode: true` is rejected in `travelBetweenImages`.\n+- Active AI/frontend emitters no longer pass `turbo_mode`.\n+- Targeted resolver tests cover rejection and safe false/undefined behavior.\n+\n+Validation:\n+\n+```bash\n+npm run test:edge:unit -- --run supabase/functions/create-task/resolvers/__tests__/travelBetweenImages.test.ts\n+```\n+\n+Result: passed.\n+\n+The full edge suite still has 11 pre-existing failures in unrelated files. Those failures should be tracked separately and should not be used as evidence that the turbo-mode fix failed.\n+\n+In `reigh-worker`:\n+\n+- Added `docs/migration-baselines.md` with RayWorker USED inventory, non-RayWorker API route inventory, the `image-upscale`/`image_upscale` mismatch, and per-task contract skeletons.\n+\n+## Lessons For Future Chains\n+\n+1. Run a repository-topology preflight before planning. If the chain root contains nested Git repos, the harness needs an explicit publish strategy for each nested repo.\n+2. Treat human gates as first-class gates. Do not convert them into executor tasks and do not let placeholders satisfy \"named owner\" criteria.\n+3. Make profile strategy visible before execution. For high-stakes chains, print all milestone profiles and bakeoff arms up front.\n+4. Require per-task evidence in executor output. Aggregate command logs are useful, but quality gates need task-local files changed and commands run.\n+5. Separate implementation artifacts from oversight artifacts. Performance reviews should not be auto-attributed to implementation tasks unless the plan explicitly included them.\n+6. Do not advance a chain just because the executor finished. The correct completion condition is executor success plus human verification where the spec requires it.\n+\n+## Open Follow-Ups\n+\n+- Publish separate PRs for `reigh-app`, `reigh-worker`, and the Megaplan harness.\n+- Assign real owners for Section 12 and non-RayWorker route decisions.\n+- Add a Megaplan chain preflight that rejects ambiguous nested-repo publish topology unless configured.\n+- Add a profile-lint command for chain specs.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/learnings/megaplan-vibecomfy-sprint-00a-2026-05-05.md\n@@\n ## Continuation Note\n@@\n - This satisfies the formal \"named owner\" gate so the chain can proceed, but later sprints must still confirm whether Peter keeps each owner role or delegates it to the actual engineering, product, infra, security, VibeComfy, and canary owners.\n+\n+## Sprint 0B Start: Critique Observability And Recovery\n+\n+While starting Sprint 0B, the chain appeared silent during critique for more than 15 minutes. A sub-agent root-cause pass showed the process was not in a Python lock deadlock. It was running parallel Hermes/OpenRouter Kimi critique calls, with open HTTPS sockets and tool activity that was buffered inside the phase subprocess.\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- The parallel Hermes critique path did not set `active_step`, so `megaplan status` reported `planned` with no active step while critique was actually running.\n+- The chain driver buffers phase output until the phase exits, so live tool activity was not visible from the parent process.\n+- Terminating the long critique produced a terminal `failed` plan state, and `override replan` could not recover from `failed`.\n+\n+Harness fixes added:\n+\n+- Parallel Hermes critique now records and clears `active_step` like the normal worker path.\n+- `override replan` can recover from `failed` so a provider interruption can be retried without abandoning the milestone.\n+- Regression tests cover both behaviors.\n+\n+Validation:\n+\n+```bash\n+PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m pytest tests/test_critique.py tests/test_gate.py tests/test_chain.py tests/test_execute.py tests/test_evaluation.py tests/test_finalize.py -q\n+```\n+\n+Result: 201 passed.\n+\n+Operational note:\n+\n+- A long critique phase can still be legitimate. The better signal is not wall-clock silence alone, but `active_step`, artifact writes, process state, provider sockets, and whether phase output is being buffered.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/learnings/megaplan-vibecomfy-sprint-00a-2026-05-05.md\n@@\n Result: strict validation passed, compile passed, and 27 focused tests passed.\n+\n+## Sprint 0C Start: Light Critique Validation Edge Case\n+\n+Sprint 0C initially started under profile `nancy`, which used Hermes DeepSeek for planning and Codex for critique. Planning completed, but critique failed validation with:\n+\n+```text\n+Critique output failed check validation: disk-defaults, structure\n+```\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- Sprint 0C robustness was `light`, so the harness expected no named robustness checks.\n+- Codex nevertheless produced useful custom `checks` (`disk-defaults`, `structure`) and concrete flags about RunPod disk defaults, the real startup-template path, and stale ready-template count.\n+- The harness treated those custom check IDs as invalid unknown checks and failed the entire phase.\n+- The failure path also left `active_step` populated even though the phase had ended and no lock was held.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Critique validation in the Megaplan harness, not the Sprint 0C implementation.\n+\n+Harness fix:\n+\n+- `validate_critique_checks(..., expected_ids=[])` now accepts custom checks when no named checks are required. Those checks can still be converted into flags by the existing flag registry path.\n+- `record_step_failure()` now clears `active_step` so failed phases do not look healthy/running in `megaplan status`.\n+\n+Validation:\n+\n+```bash\n+PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m pytest tests/test_critique.py tests/test_evaluation.py -q\n+```\n+\n+Result: 78 passed.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Published the harness fix to `peteromallet/megaplan` PR #27.\n+- Set Sprint 0C profile to `all-codex`.\n+- Re-entered the planning loop from `failed` to `planned` with `override replan`, then continued the chain.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/learnings/megaplan-vibecomfy-sprint-00a-2026-05-05.md\n@@\n Recovery:\n \n - Published the harness fix to `peteromallet/megaplan` PR #27.\n - Set Sprint 0C profile to `all-codex`.\n - Re-entered the planning loop from `failed` to `planned` with `override replan`, then continued the chain.\n+\n+## Sprint 0C Start: Critique Transcript Payload Selection Bug\n+\n+The first Sprint 0C critique failure exposed a second harness edge case after the light-mode check validation issue.\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- Codex wrote a valid `critique_output.json` with no named checks and three useful flags.\n+- The raw transcript also contained an earlier intermediate JSON object with custom `checks` IDs (`disk-defaults`, `structure`).\n+- Megaplan recovery appended direct file JSON, recovered file candidates, and raw transcript candidates into one list, then for critique chose the valid payload with the largest number of check findings.\n+- That meant raw intermediate transcript JSON could outrank the actual output file and send stale/non-canonical data into critique validation.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Critique worker recovery in the Megaplan harness, specifically Codex payload recovery after output parsing.\n+- This was not a Sprint 0C implementation error. The critique flags themselves were useful and should have led to revision.\n+\n+Harness fix:\n+\n+- `_recover_codex_payload()` now prefers a valid output file or fallback output file during normal recovery before considering raw transcript candidates.\n+- Timeout recovery keeps its older behavior by passing `prefer_output_file=False`, so partial timeout raw output can still rescue a result when Codex timed out before committing a final file.\n+- Added a regression test where `critique_output.json` contains a valid light-mode critique while raw transcript contains a tempting custom-check payload with more findings.\n+\n+Validation:\n+\n+```bash\n+PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m pytest tests/test_workers.py tests/test_critique.py tests/test_evaluation.py -q\n+```\n+\n+Result: 187 passed, with four existing deprecation warnings about must-priority criteria lacking `requires`.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Published the deeper harness fix to `peteromallet/megaplan` PR #27 as commit `b8290ca6`.\n+- Sprint 0C had already continued into revise after the first patch; this second fix prevents the same recovery bug from recurring later in the chain.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan/megaplan/workers.py\n@@\n def _normalize_worker_payload(step: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:\n+    if step == \"execute\":\n+        normalized = dict(payload)\n+        task_updates = normalized.get(\"task_updates\")\n+        if isinstance(task_updates, list):\n+            normalized_updates: list[Any] = []\n+            for update in task_updates:\n+                if not isinstance(update, dict):\n+                    normalized_updates.append(update)\n+                    continue\n+                item = dict(update)\n+                if \"task_id\" not in item and isinstance(item.get(\"id\"), str):\n+                    item[\"task_id\"] = item[\"id\"]\n+                if item.get(\"status\") == \"completed\":\n+                    item[\"status\"] = \"done\"\n+                normalized_updates.append(item)\n+            normalized[\"task_updates\"] = normalized_updates\n+        acknowledgments = normalized.get(\"sense_check_acknowledgments\")\n+        if isinstance(acknowledgments, list):\n+            normalized_acknowledgments: list[Any] = []\n+            for acknowledgment in acknowledgments:\n+                if not isinstance(acknowledgment, dict):\n+                    normalized_acknowledgments.append(acknowledgment)\n+                    continue\n+                item = dict(acknowledgment)\n+                if \"sense_check_id\" not in item and isinstance(item.get(\"id\"), str):\n+                    item[\"sense_check_id\"] = item[\"id\"]\n+                normalized_acknowledgments.append(item)\n+            normalized[\"sense_check_acknowledgments\"] = normalized_acknowledgments\n+        return normalized\n     if step == \"revise\" and \"changes_summary\" not in payload:\n         normalized = dict(payload)\n         flags_addressed = normalized.get(\"flags_addressed\", [])\n*** End Patch\n"

{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/learnings/megaplan-vibecomfy-sprint-00a-2026-05-05.md\n@@\n - Chain callback failures should reconcile the latest successful `execution_batch_N.json` back into `finalize.json` before leaving the plan failed.\n - Callback failure should clear stale `active_step`, just like normal step failure.\n - Generated pre-run user-action gates need to honor higher-priority driver/user notes, especially when the user explicitly says to do live infrastructure work directly.\n - Agent sandbox network failures should not be treated as proof of external service failure when the main shell can independently verify the service.\n+\n+## Sprint 01 Prep: Harness Callback Recovery Patch\n+\n+Before starting Sprint 01, we patched the known Sprint 0C harness gap rather than carrying it forward.\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- A chain `phase_complete` callback failure after execute could leave useful `execution_batch_N.json` evidence stranded while `finalize.json` stayed stale.\n+- Lifecycle failure recording preserved stale `active_step` metadata, so a failed plan could look as though an execute worker was still active.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Megaplan harness `auto` / `chain publish` failure boundary after `execute`.\n+- Megaplan persistence layer lifecycle failure recording.\n+\n+Harness fix:\n+\n+- Added best-effort reconciliation of the latest `execution_batch_N.json` into `finalize.json` when an execute phase-complete callback fails.\n+- Made lifecycle failure recording clear `active_step`.\n+- Added a regression test covering callback failure reconciliation with execute alias fields (`id`, `completed`) and stale active-step cleanup.\n+\n+Validation:\n+\n+```bash\n+PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m pytest tests/test_auto.py::test_execute_callback_failure_reconciles_latest_batch_and_clears_active_step tests/test_workers.py tests/test_critique.py tests/test_evaluation.py -q\n+```\n+\n+Result: 189 passed, with the same four existing deprecation warnings.\n+\n+Published:\n+\n+- `peteromallet/megaplan` PR #27, commit `a60db0d8` (`Recover execute checkpoints on callback failure`).\n*** End Patch\n"
}

{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/learnings/megaplan-vibecomfy-sprint-00a-2026-05-05.md\n@@\n - `peteromallet/megaplan` PR #27, commit `dd002808` (`Treat plan artifact writes as auto liveness`).\n \n Sprint 01 implementation status:\n@@\n - `reigh-worker` published `18b12d16` (`Add VibeComfy memory profile protocol helper`) to `banodoco/reigh-worker` branch `megaplan/vibecomfy-sprint-01-memory-profile`.\n - Review approved all must criteria; the only waived criterion was info-level real GPU VRAM/wall-clock collection for profiles 1 and 3.\n+\n+## Sprint 02 Critique: Codex Template Output Was Ignored\n+\n+Sprint 02 initially failed in critique.\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- Codex wrote a full critique into the side-effect `critique_output.json` template, with all required checks populated and concrete flags.\n+- The harness validated Codex's separate temporary `-o` structured response first. That response was only a short summary saying the critique file had been written.\n+- Because `_recover_codex_payload()` returned the short valid schema response before considering the populated template file, `handle_critique()` rejected the payload as missing completed checks for `correctness`, `scope`, `all_locations`, and `callers`.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Megaplan critique payload recovery in `workers.py`, before `handlers/critique.py` validation.\n+\n+Fix:\n+\n+- `_recover_codex_payload()` now parses the side-effect template file (`critique_output.json`, and `review_output.json` for parity) when it exists.\n+- For critique, recovery compares all valid candidates and picks the one with the strongest completed-check score: number of checks with findings, then total findings.\n+- If the actual output path is already `critique_output.json`, the existing \"prefer output file\" behavior remains, so raw transcript snippets do not outrank the intentional output file.\n+- Added regression tests for:\n+  - populated critique template beats a short schema summary;\n+  - empty template does not mask a meaningful output payload;\n+  - existing output-file preference still holds.\n+\n+Validation:\n+\n+```bash\n+PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m pytest tests/test_workers.py::test_recover_codex_payload_prefers_completed_critique_template_over_schema_summary tests/test_workers.py::test_recover_codex_payload_keeps_meaningful_critique_when_template_is_empty tests/test_workers.py::test_recover_codex_payload_prefers_valid_output_file_over_raw_transcript tests/test_auto.py::test_phase_complete_callback_skipped_after_nonzero_phase tests/test_auto.py::test_plan_liveness_mtime_uses_state_and_execution_batches tests/test_critique.py tests/test_evaluation.py -q\n+```\n+\n+Result: 83 passed, with the same four existing deprecation warnings.\n+\n+Published:\n+\n+- `peteromallet/megaplan` PR #27, commit `6de477da` (`Prefer completed critique template recovery`).\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Used `override replan` to return Sprint 02 to `planned` with the recovered critique findings as an explicit note.\n+- Reran critique with `--fresh`; it succeeded and recorded 13 critique flags.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

missing-selector WGP fallback needed a SQL-side capability source, not only Python task-type knowledge;\n+  - active task-count parity after rollback needed persisted claim-time backend/selector fields, not live selector lookup.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Sprint 06 `gate`/`critique`, before execution.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Gate forced revisions until the plan separated four concepts clearly:\n+  - live `route_backend_selectors` controls queued eligibility and rollback;\n+  - `route_backend_capabilities` controls WGP-safe missing-selector fallback;\n+  - task snapshot fields support creation observability and child pinning;\n+  - claim fields record the exact decision used for active work and accounting.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- For migration contracts, plan critique should explicitly ask whether every runtime decision has a durable source of truth in the same layer that enforces it. Python helper knowledge is not enough when SQL owns claim eligibility.\n+\n+### Review Caught Two Must-Level Execution Bugs\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- The first execute pass completed all tasks, but review found two real failures:\n+  - claim responses/logs exposed create-time `selected_backend` as if it were the live claim decision after selector rollback;\n+  - malformed or unsupported claim decisions that escaped SQL stopped the worker locally but left the already-claimed task assigned/in-progress.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Sprint 06 review phase, against T4 and T8.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Reworked `claim-next-task` and the claim RPC so live claim fields are top-level and task snapshot fields are separately named with `task_*`.\n+- Reworked worker guard behavior so malformed/unsupported escaped decisions are marked failed before execution, with retry requeue fallback if the fail update cannot be sent.\n+- Added tests for stale task snapshot response separation and fail-closed worker clearing.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- \"Field exists\" is not enough for a claim contract. Review must verify which field is live, which is historical, and what happens under rollback.\n+- Fail-closed worker behavior must include clearing the remote task state, not just returning local `ERROR`.\n+\n+### Nested Publication Guard Was Correct But Still Operationally Expensive\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- Execute succeeded, but the chain callback failed because claimed implementation files were in nested Git repos.\n+- This happened once after initial execute and again after rework execute.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Megaplan chain phase-complete callback after `execute`.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Published the nested repos first:\n+  - `reigh-app#10`\n+  - `reigh-worker#27`\n+- Reran the chain; existing harness recovery restored the plan out of terminal `failed` and continued to review.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- The guard is right: top-level commits cannot publish nested repo changes.\n+- The operational workflow should treat nested publication as a first-class post-execute step for every chain milestone that touches nested repos.\n+\n+### Transient GitHub 504 Needed Harness Retry\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- After Sprint 06 reached `done`, `gh pr view 11 --json state` failed with HTTP 504 from GitHub GraphQL.\n+- The milestone was already done, but the chain wrapper stopped because the PR state check was treated as a hard one-shot command.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Megaplan `chain.py`, PR state lookup after completion.\n+\n+Harness fix:\n+\n+- Added retry handling for transient GitHub `gh pr view` 5xx/timeout failures.\n+- Pushed to Megaplan harness PR `peteromallet/megaplan#27`, commit `5d8ba678`.\n+\n+Validation:\n+\n+```bash\n+PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m pytest tests/test_chain.py::test_pr_state_retries_transient_gh_failures tests/test_chain.py::test_enable_auto_merge_falls_back_when_repo_disallows_auto_merge tests/test_chain.py::test_run_chain_advances_when_pr_already_merged -q\n+```\n+\n+Result: 3 passed.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Network/API checks after a successful milestone should be retried when the failure class is clearly transient.\n+- The chain state had already persisted `last_state: done`; retrying avoids turning a completed milestone into manual operator work.\n*** End Patch\n"

For modules used in low-dependency tests, prefer postponed annotations or local typing-only imports.\n+\n+## Sprint 08: Orchestrated Route Lifecycle\n+\n+Plan: `sprint-8-orchestrated-route-20260506-1506`\n+\n+Outcome:\n+\n+- Megaplan plan reached `done`.\n+- Execute completed 12/12 tasks and 11/11 batches.\n+- Review passed 14/14 success criteria.\n+- Nested implementation PRs were published:\n+  - `banodoco/reigh-app#12`\n+  - `banodoco/reigh-worker#29`\n+\n+### Gate Correctly Forced Parent/Child Boundary Clarification\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- Early plan iterations were not explicit enough about the app shared `taskCreation` path and how canary route selection should be serialized into create-task requests.\n+- Without that clarification, execution could have fixed worker-side lifecycle contracts while still leaving frontend/API-created parent tasks able to drift or omit the route contract.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Sprint 08 critique/gate before execution.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Gate iterated the plan until it covered shared app task creation, selected-route serialization, create-task fail-closed behavior, parent-derived worker child snapshots, idempotency/cancellation reentry, and repair/debug output.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- For parent/child route propagation, planning must include both creation-time ingress and worker reentry. If the app path is missing, worker correctness alone is not enough.\n+\n+### Execute Timeout Killed A Healthy Long-Running Phase\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- The first execute run was still healthy, with fresh stdout and active validation, but `megaplan auto` hit the hard two-hour phase timeout and marked the plan `failed`.\n+- At failure, the plan had preserved progress through 9/12 tasks and 8/11 batches. The timeout was not caused by inactivity; it was a wall-clock cap.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Megaplan auto driver during Sprint 08 execute.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Ran `megaplan resume --plan sprint-8-orchestrated-route-20260506-1506`.\n+- Resume reused existing execution batch receipts and completed batches 9-11.\n+- Review then passed.\n+- Harness patch pushed to `peteromallet/megaplan` branch `fix/nested-repo-chain-execute-recovery`:\n+  - `megaplan/auto.py` now treats progress output or plan-artifact liveness as extending the active phase when idle timeout monitoring is enabled.\n+  - `megaplan/_core/workflow.py` now restores a runnable phase state while a failed/blocked plan is actively being resumed.\n+  - Focused tests passed: `tests/editorial_run_lifecycle.py` and related auto recovery tests, 8 total.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Auto needs to distinguish stale execution from long execution. A hard wall-clock cap is too blunt for large all-Codex execute phases that keep producing receipts and validation output.\n+- Resume must make active state visible to status consumers. Reporting `state=failed` while a resume execute is running is technically recoverable but operationally misleading and can confuse chain orchestration.\n+\n+### Chain State Did Not Reconcile After Manual Resume\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- `chain start --one` stopped when auto marked Sprint 08 failed. After manual `megaplan resume` and `megaplan review`, the plan was `done`, but chain state still recorded `last_state: failed` for Sprint 08.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Chain state persistence around a timeout-resumed milestone.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Treat the plan state as source of truth for completion.\n+- Publish nested PRs and then reconcile the top-level chain milestone before advancing.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Chain recovery should re-check the current plan state before treating a stored failed chain state as authoritative. A resumed plan can legitimately move from failed to done outside the original chain process.\n+\n+### Validation Noise Increased Cost But Did Not Block The Sprint\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- Broad validation continued to hit known unrelated or local-environment failures:\n+  - edge broad tests in `complete_task`, `timeline-import`, and `ai-timeline-agent`;\n+  - app Vitest UI failures/timeouts;\n+  - later missing local `vitest` in `node_modules/.bin`;\n+  - worker collection under local Python 3.14 missing `torch`/`httpx`.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Sprint 08 execute batches, especially final validation.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Focused suites were run and passed before broad-suite classification.\n+- The temporary mixed-backend route-drift reproduction script proved the original failure mode now returns explicit repair-required output, then was deleted.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- The cheap-to-broad validation order is essential. Focused route lifecycle tests tell us whether the sprint met intent; broad suites tell us about ambient repo health and should be documented separately unless a focused repro ties them to the sprint.\n*** End Patch\n"

> DEVELOPER

and while you're doing this have you actually been testing vibe comfy on production and runpad with the new workflows to actually validate that everything actually works for them and at the end of this are we going to have complete feature parity with what we had before in 1.2gp?

> AGENT

Not yet for the live VibeComfy proof in this current Sprint 09 execution. Up through Sprint 08 we validated contracts, routing, lifecycle guards, repair signals, and focused regression suites; Sprint 09’s final plan includes an explicit live RunPod/control-rail proof task, and I’ll make sure that is executed rather than accepting local tests as enough.

On feature parity: the chain is designed to get us to canary-ready parity for the selected USED routes, not blanket parity with every WGP capability. Sprint 09 is control-rail/travel matrix, Sprint 10 is canary readiness integration, Sprint 11 is production canary patches/runbook, and Sprint 12 hardens dual executor behavior. So the honest answer is: at the end we should have verified parity for the migration target surface and clear documented exceptions for anything intentionally WGP-only or unsupported, but I will not call it complete until the live RunPod proof and matrix evidence support that.

> AGENT

{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/learnings/megaplan-vibecomfy-sprint-00a-2026-05-05.md\n@@\n ### Detached RunPod Polling Could Wait Too Long After SSH Loss\n@@\n - Live validation harnesses need failure bounds around observability failures, not only around remote execution time. If the runner cannot poll the remote process repeatedly, that is itself a failed validation and should terminate promptly.\n - This did not prove LTX runtime parity. The right next proof remains a scoped LTX run that produces artifacts, followed by a separate Reigh-shaped travel adapter proof before any production selector promotion.\n+\n+### Chain Publish Swept In Pre-Existing Top-Level Dirt\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- After Sprint 09 review passed, `chain start --one` published PR #14 with `git add -A`.\n+- The workspace already had an unrelated dirty generated file: `packages/timeline-composition/typescript/src/effects.generated.ts`.\n+- Because the chain publisher staged everything, that unrelated import change was included in the squash merge even though the plan audit had already flagged it as an unclaimed file.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Megaplan chain phase-complete/publish logic, specifically the milestone commit phase after a completed plan.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Reverted the accidental generated-file change on top-level `main` with commit `61b0770`.\n+- Patched and pushed the Megaplan harness (`peteromallet/megaplan` commit `693a8b21`) so chain publish records dirty paths at chain start and resets those pre-existing root-file changes out of each milestone commit after `git add -A`.\n+- Added regression coverage in `tests/test_chain.py` for preserving pre-existing dirty root files while still committing planned milestone changes.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Chain publish must treat the starting worktree as user-owned state. A plan can produce valid changes while unrelated local dirt exists, and the publisher must not convert that local dirt into a PR just because it uses broad staging.\n+- The audit warnings were useful but came too late. Publish-time staging needs its own guard, not just post-execute advisory output.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/learnings/megaplan-vibecomfy-sprint-00a-2026-05-05.md\n@@\n ### Critique Recovery Trusted Stdout Over A Valid Output File\n \n What went wrong:\n@@\n - For file-contract workers, the harness should prefer a valid declared output artifact over opportunistic stdout extraction whenever those channels disagree.\n - Check-ID validation is still valuable, but the recovery layer must apply it to the artifact of record before declaring the run failed.\n+\n+### Execute Auto-Loop Continued After A Blocked Task\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- Sprint 11A execution correctly blocked T9 because the finalized plan treated live canary trigger details as a user-supplied before-execute action.\n+- The auto execute loop then continued into T1 even though T1 depended on the blocked T9.\n+- Megaplan was explicitly treating previously blocked task IDs as satisfied for batch scheduling, which let dependent batches run after a hard stop.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Megaplan execute auto-loop batching in `megaplan/execute/core.py`.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Stopped the active chain driver before it spent more work on blocked dependent batches.\n+- Replanned Sprint 11A so the agent, not the user, owns route inventory and live RunPod/Reigh-shaped evidence gathering.\n+- Patched and pushed the live Megaplan harness (`peteromallet/megaplan` commit `4a7a6969`) so auto execute immediately returns blocked when any task is already blocked.\n+- Added regression coverage proving the worker is not invoked after an existing blocked task; full `tests/test_execute.py` passed.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- A blocked task is not a satisfied dependency. If the orchestration wants out-of-band resolution, it should require an explicit replan or task status change, not silently schedule downstream work.\n+- User-action gates should be reserved for genuinely human-only operations. If the chain owner has instructed the agent to gather live production/RunPod evidence, that work belongs in executable tasks, not in `Before Execute`.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

> TOOL

tool_use apply_patch
```json
{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/vibecomfy/scripts/runpod_route_validate.py\n@@\n DEFAULT_OUT_DIR = Path(\"out\") / \"reigh_route_validation\"\n DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 1800\n DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 30\n+DEFAULT_ENV_FILES = (\n+    ROOT / \".env\",\n+    ROOT.parent / \"reigh-worker\" / \".env\",\n+)\n@@\n def _load_fixture(path: Path) -> dict:\n     return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n \n \n+def _load_env_file(path: Path) -> None:\n+    if not path.exists():\n+        return\n+    for raw_line in path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").splitlines():\n+        line = raw_line.strip()\n+        if not line or line.startswith(\"#\") or \"=\" not in line:\n+            continue\n+        key, value = line.split(\"=\", 1)\n+        key = key.strip()\n+        value = value.strip()\n+        if value and value[0] == value[-1] and value[0] in {'\"', \"'\"}:\n+            value = value[1:-1]\n+        os.environ.setdefault(key, value)\n+\n+\n+def load_default_env_files(paths: Sequence[Path] = DEFAULT_ENV_FILES) -> None:\n+    for path in paths:\n+        _load_env_file(path)\n+\n+\n def resolve_route_template(\n@@\n async def async_main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:\n     args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)\n+    load_default_env_files()\n     if not args.route_key and not args.task_type:\n         args.route_key = \"z_image_turbo\"\n*** End Patch\n"
}

I’m fixing two concrete causes now. First, the live-test fresh path needs to provision VibeComfy on the worker pod when `--backend vibecomfy` is selected; cloning only `Reigh-Worker` leaves the VibeComfy preflight incomplete. Second, the worker’s preflight metadata path should use the service key when present, even if the task auth mode is PAT/worker, otherwise readiness metadata gets a 401 and the harness waits blindly.

The queue proof now reaches actual execution and fails for a new concrete runtime mismatch: VibeComfy’s isolated venv pulled a PyTorch build requiring a newer NVIDIA driver than the RunPod image has. The standalone VibeComfy proof passed because it used the image’s system Python/Torch. So the right fix is not a new pod type; it is to install VibeComfy into the system Python 3.11 environment on this image, preserving the image’s compatible Torch/CUDA stack.

started_at, 1),\n+                timeout_sec=timeout_sec,\n+                fresh_polls=consecutive_fresh_polls,\n+            )\n+            next_progress_at = now + progress_every_sec\n+\n         time.sleep(interval_sec)\n*** End Patch\n"

Promotion should stay canary-scoped and route-specific. |\n+| Section 3A support-report metadata | rejected | Travel/Section 3A rows still lack VibeComfy adapter parity and live Reigh-shaped proof. |\n+| Worker claim guard | no new patch required by this proof | Claim behavior was exercised through the queue proof; no separate guard defect was found for `z_image_turbo`. |\n+| Task-count selected-pool visibility | no new patch required by this proof | The live case proved execution/completion, not a need for aggregate count behavior changes. |\n+| Orchestrator pool / stale-worker behavior | rejected | No orchestrator route is promoted; travel/join/edit-video parents remain WGP-only or blocked. |\n+| Completion | no new patch required by this proof | The route completed and produced generation artifacts through the existing completion path. |\n+| Billing | no new patch required by this proof | No billing-specific defect was observed in this canary route proof. |\n+| Worker adapter behavior | patched in live harness/runtime support | Worker live proof required VibeComfy provisioning, Python 3.11/system Torch selection, and service-client preflight metadata fixes. |\n+\n+## Required Next Gate\n+\n+Before production promotion beyond canary consideration:\n+\n+- Confirm the selector patch is exactly scoped to `z_image_turbo`.\n+- Keep WGP rollback available for the same route.\n+- Do not infer support for Qwen image, image-to-image, edit, upscale, video,\n+  travel, join, stitch, or other routes from this proof.\n+- Require the same selected-template plus Reigh-shaped queue proof for each\n+  additional route before promotion.\n+\n+Sprint 11A's usable boundary is therefore narrow: `z_image_turbo` can move to\n+the next canary promotion decision; all other routes stay fail-closed.\n*** End Patch\n"

If the chain owner has instructed the agent to gather live production/RunPod evidence, that work belongs in executable tasks, not in `Before Execute`.\n+\n+### Sprint 11A Initially Stopped At Fail-Closed Evidence Instead Of Recovering Live Proof\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- Sprint 11A execution produced useful endpoint inventory and validation infrastructure, but the first live proof pass failed before producing production-relevant evidence.\n+- The first VibeComfy selected-template proof failed because the route validator only read the process environment and did not load the adjacent Reigh worker `.env` file that held the live RunPod settings.\n+- The first Reigh-shaped queue proof failed during Supabase DNS/connect lookup. A later direct token probe succeeded, so that specific failure was transient provider/network behavior, not a persistent auth problem.\n+- Manual recovery then exposed real harness and runtime defects that the first execution result had not diagnosed: missing VibeComfy provisioning, wrong Python boundary, incompatible isolated Torch install, PAT-vs-service-client preflight metadata, and secret-bearing RunPod SDK stdout.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Execution batch T4 live proof.\n+- Post-execute sense-check and manual retry uncovered the deeper failures.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Patched VibeComfy `scripts/runpod_route_validate.py` so it loads env from `vibecomfy/.env` and neighboring `reigh-worker/.env` without overriding explicit shell env.\n+- Patched Reigh worker live fresh harness to clone/install VibeComfy for `REIGH_BACKEND=vibecomfy` and export the required `VIBECOMFY_*` env.\n+- Patched Reigh worker preflight metadata publication to use the service client when the service key is available.\n+- Patched the live VibeComfy runtime path to use system `python3.11` and the RunPod image's compatible Torch stack instead of an isolated venv that pulled an incompatible CUDA/Torch combination.\n+- Patched runpod-lifecycle to suppress SDK stdout during pod creation so secret-bearing raw responses are not printed.\n+- Reran all three proofs successfully: VibeComfy selected-template RunPod proof, Reigh-shaped VibeComfy queue proof, and WGP rollback proof for `z_image_turbo`.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- A fail-closed plan result is not enough when the user's directive is to get to live proof. The next action should classify whether the blocker is provider availability, credentials/env loading, harness coverage, or product runtime behavior, then fix the fixable layer.\n+- Route promotion evidence must be route-specific and Reigh-shaped. `z_image_turbo` proof does not imply parity for Qwen image, image-to-image, edit, upscale, video, travel, join, stitch, or orchestrator routes.\n+- Live harnesses need to load the same env sources humans use during local operations, while still allowing explicit shell exports to override them.\n+\n+### RunPod Lifecycle Printed Secret-Bearing Pod Create Responses\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- RunPod's SDK printed a raw pod create response that included container env values.\n+- The live proof path injects service-role and worker credentials into pod env, so raw SDK stdout became a secret exposure risk in local logs.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- `runpod-lifecycle` pod creation wrapper during Sprint 11A manual recovery.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Suppressed stdout/stderr around the SDK create call and logged only sanitized debug metadata.\n+- Added regression coverage proving create-pod does not echo env values to stdout.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Any lifecycle layer that passes env vars to a provider must treat provider SDK output as untrusted. Do not assume SDKs redact values.\n+- Secret redaction belongs in the shared lifecycle wrapper, not just in the caller, because every live harness will otherwise need to remember the same defensive behavior.\n+\n+### Reigh Fresh Live Harness Did Not Provision VibeComfy\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- The fresh live worker proof cloned and installed Reigh-Worker but did not clone VibeComfy.\n+- `REIGH_BACKEND=vibecomfy` then failed runtime preflight because the worker could not find the VibeComfy manifests and templates.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Reigh worker `scripts/live_test` fresh variant during Sprint 11A manual recovery.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Added VibeComfy clone/install support to the fresh variant when the selected backend is `vibecomfy`.\n+- Exported `VIBECOMFY_CWD`, `VIBECOMFY_PATH`, and `VIBECOMFY_PYTHON` into the live worker env.\n+- Added focused live harness tests for required VibeComfy manifest validation.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- A backend selector proof must provision all backend dependencies inside the proof environment. It is not enough for the component to exist elsewhere in the monorepo or on the developer machine.\n+- Worker preflight was useful here: it failed before task execution and turned a missing dependency into a clear route-runtime blocker.\n+\n+### VibeComfy Python And Torch Boundaries Were Easy To Get Wrong\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- Reigh-Worker's live install uses a Python 3.10 virtualenv, but VibeComfy requires Python 3.11.\n+- Switching to an isolated VibeComfy Python 3.11 venv then pulled a newer Torch/CUDA combination incompatible with the RunPod image driver.\n+- Standalone VibeComfy proof passed because it used the image's existing compatible Python 3.11/Torch environment, while the first Reigh-shaped integration path accidentally changed that runtime boundary.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Reigh-shaped VibeComfy queue proof during Sprint 11A manual recovery.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Kept Reigh-Worker on its own install path.\n+- Installed and ran VibeComfy through system `python3.11`, preserving the RunPod image's compatible Torch stack.\n+- Documented this as part of the live proof boundary rather than treating it as a generic install concern.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Integration proofs must preserve the runtime contract of the component being integrated. A clean venv is often desirable locally, but GPU images frequently rely on pre-installed driver-compatible Torch stacks.\n+- Future VibeComfy live harnesses should explicitly report Python, Torch, CUDA, and driver versions before execution so incompatibilities are diagnosed before a paid task waits and fails.\n+\n+### Live Harness UX Was Too Silent During Long Remote Phases\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- During pod creation, SSH readiness, apt install, uv sync, VibeComfy install, heartbeat wait, and matrix execution, the local CLI could sit silent for long stretches.\n+- Silence made normal provider boot/install latency look like a hang and made it harder to distinguish RunPod availability from harness failure.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Reigh worker live fresh harness while recovering Sprint 11A.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Added phase start/completion/failure logs around pod creation, SSH open, Reigh clone/install, VibeComfy clone/install, worker launch, heartbeat wait, matrix execution, and report writing.\n+- Added periodic heartbeat wait progress logging.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Live proof tooling needs operator-facing progress at every paid or remote boundary. A good live harness should classify \"waiting for provider\", \"installing dependencies\", \"worker launched but no heartbeat\", \"task queued\", and \"task executing\" without requiring a second terminal or manual provider inspection.\n+- The next UX improvement should stream or summarize remote command output safely, with secret redaction, rather than only logging local phase boundaries.\n*** End Patch\n"

{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/learnings/megaplan-vibecomfy-sprint-00a-2026-05-05.md\n@@\n ### Live Harness UX Was Too Silent During Long Remote Phases\n@@\n - Live proof tooling needs operator-facing progress at every paid or remote boundary. A good live harness should classify \"waiting for provider\", \"installing dependencies\", \"worker launched but no heartbeat\", \"task queued\", and \"task executing\" without requiring a second terminal or manual provider inspection.\n - The next UX improvement should stream or summarize remote command output safely, with secret redaction, rather than only logging local phase boundaries.\n+\n+### Chain Fallback Squash Merge Persisted Stale PR State\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- Sprint 11A merged successfully through the chain runner's fallback immediate squash merge path because the repository does not allow GitHub auto-merge.\n+- The persisted chain state still recorded the completed milestone's `pr_state` as `open`.\n+- GitHub showed PR #16 as merged, so this was a Megaplan state bookkeeping defect, not a GitHub merge failure.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Megaplan `chain start --one` milestone completion after `gh pr merge --auto` failed with \"Auto merge is not allowed\" and the runner fell back to `gh pr merge --squash`.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Patched and pushed Megaplan (`peteromallet/megaplan` commit `741c3a28`) so `_enable_auto_merge` returns `merged` when the fallback immediate squash merge succeeds and returns `open` only when deferred auto-merge is enabled.\n+- Updated chain tests for the fallback merge result and branch PR commit path.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Chain state should represent the durable provider result, not the code path name. \"Auto merge unavailable\" plus successful immediate merge is a completed merge.\n+- Persisted orchestration metadata needs post-action state fidelity because later operators use chain status to decide whether they are resuming, waiting, or advancing.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/learnings/megaplan-vibecomfy-sprint-00a-2026-05-05.md\n@@\n ### Chain Fallback Squash Merge Persisted Stale PR State\n@@\n - Chain state should represent the durable provider result, not the code path name. \"Auto merge unavailable\" plus successful immediate merge is a completed merge.\n - Persisted orchestration metadata needs post-action state fidelity because later operators use chain status to decide whether they are resuming, waiting, or advancing.\n+\n+### Execute Auto-Loop Also Continued After Newly Blocked Tasks\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- An earlier Megaplan fix stopped execute when a plan already had blocked tasks at the start of an execute call.\n+- Sprint 11B exposed the adjacent edge case: task `T7` became blocked during batch 1, then dependent `T1` and `T2` were also marked blocked, but the same execute auto-loop kept scheduling later batches.\n+- That produced misleading partial execution for a plan that had explicitly said \"mark blocked and stop\" when pre-execute actions could not be verified.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Megaplan execute auto-loop during Sprint 11B production canary runbook/dashboard execution.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Stopped the active chain run before it could publish misleading partial artifacts.\n+- Patched and pushed Megaplan (`peteromallet/megaplan` commit `34f4f404`) so execute treats worker-reported `status=blocked` as a hard stop within the same auto-loop.\n+- Added regression coverage for both pre-existing blocked tasks and newly blocked tasks created by a batch; full `tests/test_execute.py` passed.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Blocked is a terminal scheduler signal, not just a task-level annotation. The scheduler must stop both when a blocked task exists before execution and when a worker creates one mid-execution.\n+- Plans that use `Before Execute` gates are especially likely to create this condition, so blocked-task semantics need to be enforced in the harness rather than relying on executor prose.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/learnings/megaplan-vibecomfy-sprint-00a-2026-05-05.md\n@@\n ### Execute Auto-Loop Also Continued After Newly Blocked Tasks\n@@\n - Blocked is a terminal scheduler signal, not just a task-level annotation. The scheduler must stop both when a blocked task exists before execution and when a worker creates one mid-execution.\n - Plans that use `Before Execute` gates are especially likely to create this condition, so blocked-task semantics need to be enforced in the harness rather than relying on executor prose.\n+\n+### Deferred Auto-Merge Command Can Merge Immediately\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- Sprint 11B completed and GitHub showed PR #17 as merged, but Megaplan persisted the chain milestone's `pr_state` as `open`.\n+- This was a different merge-state edge case than Sprint 11A. The `gh pr merge --auto --squash --delete-branch` command returned success, but GitHub merged the PR immediately instead of leaving it in a deferred auto-merge state.\n+- Megaplan assumed that a successful `--auto` command always meant \"open and waiting for auto-merge\", so the chain status underreported completion.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Megaplan chain publish/advance after Sprint 11B production canary runbook/dashboard completion.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Verified GitHub PR #17 directly with `gh pr view`, which reported `state=MERGED` and `mergedAt=2026-05-07T00:23:30Z`.\n+- Patched and pushed Megaplan (`peteromallet/megaplan` commit `90ad061c`) so the successful auto-merge path immediately re-queries PR state and records `merged` when GitHub has already merged the PR.\n+- Added regression coverage for the immediate-success auto-merge path; targeted chain tests passed.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- A provider command's flag name is not a durable state transition. Even `--auto` can resolve synchronously when all merge requirements are already satisfied.\n+- Chain publishers should always reconcile provider state after write operations that may be asynchronous or synchronous depending on repository settings and branch protection.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/learnings/megaplan-vibecomfy-sprint-00a-2026-05-05.md\n@@\n ### Deferred Auto-Merge Command Can Merge Immediately\n@@\n - A provider command's flag name is not a durable state transition. Even `--auto` can resolve synchronously when all merge requirements are already satisfied.\n - Chain publishers should always reconcile provider state after write operations that may be asynchronous or synchronous depending on repository settings and branch protection.\n+\n+### Sprint 12 Chain Startup Produced an Empty PR Before Visible Phase Output\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- Starting Sprint 12 through `megaplan chain start --one` appeared silent for several minutes.\n+- Process sampling showed the chain driver alive with reader threads and sleep, but no console output had reached the operator.\n+- After terminating the silent parent process, chain state showed a new Sprint 12 plan and PR #18 had already been created, while the plan itself was still only in critique.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Megaplan chain driver startup for `sprint-12-dual-executor-hardening`.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Switched from the chain wrapper to explicit phase commands for the active plan: `critique`, `gate`, `revise`, `critique`, `gate`, `finalize`, and `execute`.\n+- Reused the same Sprint 12 plan and branch rather than starting over, avoiding duplicated PRs or duplicated plan artifacts.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- The chain driver can create a branch/PR before the milestone plan is complete. That is not necessarily wrong, but it creates confusing visible GitHub state when the operator has no phase output yet.\n+- Future chain UX should emit an immediate line after each durable action: plan initialized, branch checked out, PR created/reused, active plan phase, and next status command. This should happen before long-running model phases.\n+\n+### Review Can Fail Without Repository Inspection And Succeed On Retry\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- The first Sprint 12 review returned `Blocked: incomplete review coverage (0/14 task verdicts, 0/14 sense checks)`.\n+- This was not a code failure; the reviewer attempted to answer from metadata without inspecting the workspace diff, and Megaplan correctly rejected the review as incomplete.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Megaplan review phase after Sprint 12 execution.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Reran `megaplan review`; the second attempt inspected nested worktrees and approved all must criteria.\n+- Independently reran the key worker, orchestrator, app route-contract, dashboard, alert, and readiness checks instead of relying only on the reviewer verdict.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Review self-audit is useful: rejecting a no-inspection review prevented a false approval.\n+- The harness should treat \"0 task verdicts / 0 sense checks\" as a retryable review-attempt failure with clearer operator guidance, not as a normal blocked milestone.\n+\n+### Reigh Worker Optional Bootstrap Was Too Narrow For Lightweight Tests\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- Sprint 12 validation of `reigh-worker/tests/test_template_routing.py` failed after the route tests had passed.\n+- Later tests imported `source`, whose package bootstrap best-effort imports WGP transformer patches.\n+- The local lightweight test stubs made `huggingface_hub` fail while defining `HfHubHTTPError(HTTPError, OSError)`, raising `TypeError: Cannot create a consistent method resolution order for bases Exception, OSError`.\n+- The bootstrap only caught `ImportError` and `AttributeError`, so an optional GPU/WGP patch path broke route and claim tests unrelated to transformers.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- `reigh-worker/source/__init__.py` during Sprint 12 local validation.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Replaced repeated narrow `try/except` bootstrap imports with `_import_optional_bootstrap(...)` and caught `Exception` for these optional registration imports only.\n+- Reran `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m pytest tests/test_template_routing.py -q`; the suite passed: 79 passed, 1 warning.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Optional bootstrap code must be truly optional. If a package-level import exists only to register dynamic modules or patches, it should not make unrelated route/claim tests depend on the full GPU model stack.\n+- Broad exception handling is usually too blunt, but it is appropriate at a clearly named optional-bootstrap boundary when the alternative is importing heavyweight model libraries for every lightweight package import.\n*** End Patch\n"

Publisher staging has to respect claimed plan files, not only timestamps or pre-phase dirtiness.\n+- The chain should probably surface a warning when a milestone PR has no diff after a `done` phase but the plan claims root-level files; that would catch empty milestone merges before GitHub merge.\n*** End Patch\n"

> AGENT

Before publishing I’m fixing one more chain publisher edge case: after a nested repo is committed, the top-level repo only sees a gitlink change. If that gitlink was dirty before publish, the publisher can wrongly reset it as “preexisting unclaimed” even though the plan claimed files inside it. This is the same class of issue that made Sprint 12 docs disappear, just for nested repos.

{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/learnings/megaplan-vibecomfy-sprint-00a-2026-05-05.md\n@@\n ### Manual Execute Then Chain Resume Can Drop Claimed Root Files\n@@\n - \"Pre-existing dirty\" and \"plan output\" are not mutually exclusive when a plan is driven manually and later resumed by the chain. Publisher staging has to respect claimed plan files, not only timestamps or pre-phase dirtiness.\n - The chain should probably surface a warning when a milestone PR has no diff after a `done` phase but the plan claims root-level files; that would catch empty milestone merges before GitHub merge.\n+\n+### Sprint 12B Packaging Smoke Exposed Absolute Symlinks In The Sdist\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- Sprint 12B's hard `[agent]` packaging smoke initially failed after dependency installation was recovered.\n+- `python -m build` failed while building the sdist because archived files under `megaplan/agent/auto_improve/iterations/*/results` were absolute symlinks into a local Hermes results directory.\n+- The wheel target already excluded the archived auto-improve iterations, but the sdist did not. The package could therefore pass wheel-oriented local checks while failing the source distribution path.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Sprint 12B task T4, pyproject dependency dedupe and fresh Hermes `[agent]` smoke.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Added a global Hatch build exclude for `megaplan/agent/auto_improve/iterations/**`, keeping the archived local iteration symlinks out of both sdist and wheel builds.\n+- Reran the hard gate: `python -m build` produced both sdist and wheel, fresh `pip install -e '.[agent]'` succeeded in `/tmp/megaplan-agent-smoke`, `_import_hermes_runtime()` succeeded, and `model_tools` imported.\n+- Published the cleanup and inventory in `peteromallet/megaplan` commit `97fb09e6`.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Packaging tests need to exercise sdist and wheel, not just editable installs. Symlinks and vendored archives are especially likely to differ between those paths.\n+- If a vendored tool contains local experimental archives, exclude them at the build-system level instead of relying on wheel-only excludes.\n+\n+### Resolved Out-Of-Band Blockers Have No First-Class Resume Path\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- Sprint 12B T4 was marked `blocked` after the initial packaging smoke failed.\n+- After the underlying issue was fixed and the hard gate passed manually, rerunning `megaplan execute` refused to continue because `finalize.json` still contained `status=blocked` for T4.\n+- That behavior is correct for normal dependency safety, but there is no first-class command to mark a blocked task resolved out-of-band with evidence and continue pending dependent tasks.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Megaplan execute resume after Sprint 12B T4 packaging-smoke recovery.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Recorded the out-of-band T4 resolution directly in the plan artifacts, marked T4/T6/T7 done with command evidence, regenerated `final.md`, and reran review.\n+- Review initially caught two real cleanup-boundary issues; after removing the unrelated active-step code change and documenting deferred/post-canary timing, review passed with no rework items.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- The harness needs an explicit operator-safe recovery path, for example `megaplan override resolve-task --task T4 --status done --evidence ...`, that updates `finalize.json`, `final.md`, and state history atomically.\n+- Without that path, operators have to choose between unsafe JSON hand edits or needless replanning after a blocker is already genuinely resolved.\n+\n+### Manual Nested Repo Commits Can Drop Claimed Gitlinks\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- Sprint 12B changed files inside the nested `megaplan-fix` repo, then committed and pushed that nested repo separately.\n+- At the top-level Reigh workspace, the only intended publishable diff was the `megaplan-fix` gitlink.\n+- The chain publisher already knew how to keep claimed root files, but not how to keep a pre-existing dirty gitlink for a nested repo whose internal files were claimed by the plan. That could have produced another empty or partial milestone PR.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Megaplan chain publish path for Sprint 12B after nested repo commit/push.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Patched and pushed Megaplan (`peteromallet/megaplan` commit `b3742025`) so `_commit_and_push_phase` treats claimed nested repo roots as claimed top-level publish paths.\n+- Added regression coverage with a real submodule/gitlink: the claimed nested gitlink is committed while unrelated pre-existing root dirt remains unstaged.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- A plan's claimed file paths need to project onto the top-level publishable object. For normal files that is the file path; for nested repos it is the repo gitlink.\n+- Chain publishers must reason at both levels or they will protect unrelated user dirt by accidentally dropping the actual nested-repo output.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

This is\n+        # common for embedded runs whose local server shuts down immediately\n+        # after returning outputs; do not let a final /system_stats miss turn\n+        # a successful run into a false crash report.\n+        if st.stop_reason == \"completed\":\n+            return \"completed\", \"stop reason was 'completed' but no execution termination event was seen\"\n+\n         # crashed: poll loop ran but /system_stats stopped responding.\n         # Only declare crashed if we did at least one sample. If the server was\n         # never reachable, fall through to missing_event_stream below.\n         if self._stats_responsive is False and self._vram_samples:\n             return \"crashed\", \"/system_stats stopped responding\"\n@@\n-        # Fallback: \"in_progress\" — nothing alarming yet. }

{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/learnings/megaplan-vibecomfy-sprint-00a-2026-05-05.md\n@@\n ### Manual Nested Repo Commits Can Drop Claimed Gitlinks\n@@\n - A plan's claimed file paths need to project onto the top-level publishable object. For normal files that is the file path; for nested repos it is the repo gitlink.\n - Chain publishers must reason at both levels or they will protect unrelated user dirt by accidentally dropping the actual nested-repo output.\n+\n+### VibeComfy Watchdog Misclassified Completed Embedded Runs As Crashed\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- Post-chain live RunPod validation for `z_image_turbo` generated the expected PNG and exited successfully, but the evidence report included a warning: `watchdog diagnosis=crashed ... stop_reason=completed and outputs exist`.\n+- The run itself was good. The embedded Comfy server shut down after returning outputs, and the watchdog later observed `/system_stats` as unavailable.\n+- Watchdog diagnosis checked `/system_stats stopped responding` before honoring the caller's successful `stop_reason=completed`, so a normal shutdown looked like a crash.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- VibeComfy `vibecomfy/runtime/watchdog.py` during RunPod route validation on 2026-05-07.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Patched VibeComfy so `stop_reason=completed` is diagnosed as completed before the post-shutdown `/system_stats` branch can classify it as crashed.\n+- Added regression coverage in `tests/test_watchdog.py`.\n+- Reran `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m pytest tests/test_watchdog.py tests/test_runpod_runner.py -q`: `33 passed`.\n+- Reran live RunPod `z_image_turbo` selected-template validation on pod `8oxw2matooidlz`: pass, one 1024x1024 PNG, warnings=0, watchdog diagnosis=completed, pod terminated.\n+- Published and merged VibeComfy PR #6 (`Avoid false crash watchdog reports after completed runs`).\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Reporting code needs to distinguish \"server disappeared after successful embedded completion\" from \"server disappeared mid-run\".\n+- RunPod reports should not only mark pass/fail; they should keep surfacing contradictory evidence. The original warning was useful because it exposed a UX bug without hiding the successful media output.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/learnings/megaplan-vibecomfy-sprint-00a-2026-05-05.md\n@@\n ### VibeComfy Watchdog Misclassified Completed Embedded Runs As Crashed\n@@\n - Reporting code needs to distinguish \"server disappeared after successful embedded completion\" from \"server disappeared mid-run\".\n - RunPod reports should not only mark pass/fail; they should keep surfacing contradictory evidence. The original warning was useful because it exposed a UX bug without hiding the successful media output.\n+\n+### WGP Live Matrix Was Blocked By A VibeComfy-Only Preflight\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- The first post-chain WGP live worker matrix started a real RunPod pod (`hflyg1k3b2ckwq`) and installed Reigh Worker successfully.\n+- The worker never heartbeated because startup preflight failed with `failed=vibecomfy_custom_nodes_manifest`.\n+- This was a WGP baseline run (`REIGH_BACKEND=wgp`), so requiring VibeComfy's custom-node coverage manifest was the wrong default. It turned a VibeComfy readiness check into a blocker for rollback/baseline proof.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Reigh Worker `source/runtime/worker/preflight.py`, during the fresh RunPod live-test harness `wait_worker_ready` phase on 2026-05-07.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Terminated the stuck RunPod pod to avoid wasting runtime.\n+- Patched Reigh Worker so VibeComfy preflight is required by default only when `backend=vibecomfy`; `REIGH_PREFLIGHT_REQUIRE_VIBECOMFY=1` can still force the check for explicit diagnostic runs.\n+- Added regression coverage for both WGP default behavior and the forced-check override.\n+- Reran:\n+  - `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m pytest tests/runtime/test_worker_preflight.py -q`: `7 passed`.\n+  - `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m pytest scripts/live_test/tests/test_primitives.py -q`: `30 passed`.\n+- Pushed Reigh Worker commit `84353f8f` to `megaplan/vibecomfy-sprint-09-control-rail-travel-matrix`, then restarted the WGP live matrix on a fresh pod.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Rollback and baseline validation paths must not depend on the experimental backend being installed perfectly. Otherwise the fallback evidence can be blocked by the thing it is meant to fall back from.\n+- Preflight checks need backend-aware requiredness, plus explicit environment overrides for deeper operator diagnostics.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/learnings/megaplan-vibecomfy-sprint-00a-2026-05-05.md\n@@\n ### WGP Live Matrix Was Blocked By A VibeComfy-Only Preflight\n@@\n - Rollback and baseline validation paths must not depend on the experimental backend being installed perfectly. Otherwise the fallback evidence can be blocked by the thing it is meant to fall back from.\n - Preflight checks need backend-aware requiredness, plus explicit environment overrides for deeper operator diagnostics.\n+\n+### Live Travel Smoke Accidentally Exercised Prompt Enhancement\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- After the preflight fix, the WGP live matrix began processing `travel_orchestrator_wan2_1seg` on pod `i307ly5qhpbhrr`.\n+- The fixture inherited `enhance_prompt=True`, so the worker started downloading `Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct` (~16GB) before segment generation.\n+- That did not match the directive: WGP prompt enhancement/pre-run text is already known and should not block or dominate VibeComfy/WGP route validation.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Reigh Worker `scripts/live_test/matrix.py`, `_build_wan_travel_fixture`, during the `run_matrix` phase on 2026-05-07.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Terminated pod `i307ly5qhpbhrr`.\n+- Cancelled the inserted live-test task `a2d125c2-3505-4eb2-99bb-7d2412695c0a` in Supabase with an explicit superseded-by-rerun error message.\n+- Patched the travel live-test fixture to set `enhance_prompt=False` and keep `enhanced_prompts_expanded=[\"\"]`.\n+- Added a regression asserting the live travel payload will not trigger prompt-enhancement downloads.\n+- Reran `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m pytest scripts/live_test/tests/test_primitives.py tests/runtime/test_worker_preflight.py -q`: `38 passed`.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Live smoke fixtures should suppress optional heavyweight preprocessors unless the test case is explicitly about that preprocessor.\n+- The matrix needs a clearer distinction between route execution proof and full product workflow proof; otherwise a route smoke can spend most of its time validating unrelated setup.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/learnings/megaplan-vibecomfy-sprint-00a-2026-05-05.md\n@@\n ### Live Travel Smoke Accidentally Exercised Prompt Enhancement\n@@\n - Live smoke fixtures should suppress optional heavyweight preprocessors unless the test case is explicitly about that preprocessor.\n - The matrix needs a clearer distinction between route execution proof and full product workflow proof; otherwise a route smoke can spend most of its time validating unrelated setup.\n+\n+### Travel Orchestrator Live Fixtures Missed The Parent Route Contract\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- The post-fix WGP live matrix completed 7/9 cases, but both `travel_orchestrator` parent cases failed immediately while spawning child tasks.\n+- Error: `Missing or malformed parent params.route_contract`.\n+- The harness was inserting parent orchestrator rows directly into Supabase without the create-task route snapshot fields that the app normally stamps. The worker correctly failed closed because child route pinning depends on the parent's persisted route contract.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Reigh Worker `scripts/live_test/matrix.py`, `travel_orchestrator_wan2_1seg` and `travel_orchestrator_ltx`, during the `run_matrix` phase on pod `v46wbqkjnlbpwg`.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Patched the travel parent matrix cases to stamp `[REDACTED]`, `support_state=wgp_only`, and the normal runtime route contract.\n+- Added regression coverage proving travel live payloads include `params.route_contract`.\n+- Reran `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m pytest scripts/live_test/tests/test_primitives.py -q`: `32 passed`.\n+- Next step is to rerun the two failed travel parent cases only, rather than repeating the seven passing cases.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- A live harness that bypasses app create-task has to recreate the create-time route contract exactly, especially for parent/orchestrator tasks that later create child rows.\n+- Fail-closed route pinning worked as intended; the bug was the harness failing to provide production-shaped parent inputs.\n*** End Patch\n"

Root cause is narrowing: the live harness considered the worker “ready” on heartbeat alone, but the worker only writes heartbeat before the long WGP import/task-queue startup path. That lets the harness insert and start timing tasks while the worker still is not ready to claim. I’m going to fix the readiness gate to require preflight `ready_for_tasks`, then restart or resume validation on the same pod once this run reaches a clean point.
