```json
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/learnings/megaplan-vibecomfy-sprint-00a-2026-05-05.md\n@@\n ### Travel Orchestrator Live Fixtures Missed The Parent Route Contract\n@@\n - A live harness that bypasses app create-task has to recreate the create-time route contract exactly, especially for parent/orchestrator tasks that later create child rows.\n - Fail-closed route pinning worked as intended; the bug was the harness failing to provide production-shaped parent inputs.\n+\n+### Orchestrator Parent Polling Missed Child Outputs\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- The focused rerun of `travel_orchestrator_wan2_1seg` and `travel_orchestrator_ltx` initially reported `0/2` even though the worker completed child segment generations and uploaded child MP4 outputs.\n+- The live harness judged the parent row too narrowly. For orchestrator tasks, the observable final media can live on child tasks or child generations rather than directly on the parent task row.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Reigh Worker `scripts/live_test` result collection, during the focused travel parent rerun on pod `mnll3jnorpxyxv`.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Patched the live harness to link orchestrator child outputs back to the parent case.\n+- Repolled the existing parent task families:\n+  - `travel_orchestrator_wan2_1seg`: parent task `367cbf14-e993-40ab-bb09-969bd9bb68db`, generation `98b9f1a6-868a-4d98-987d-a48388725c49`, child output under task `b6addd18-fcd7-4ffe-a4a8-41e35739bd14`.\n+  - `travel_orchestrator_ltx`: parent task `fd23b18b-aabf-4d6d-ad2c-af3b48722b87`, generation `a23ac486-d26d-43ee-bacc-edc0bc3f814e`, child output under task `324c03cc-ee9c-4718-9a0c-f4595c1baa2a`.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Live validation needs task-family semantics, not just single-row semantics. Parent orchestrators, child segment tasks, and final stitch tasks are one product action and should be reported that way.\n+\n+### Missing WGP Direct Route Coverage Hid App-Used Surface Area\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- After the first WGP matrix, the route coverage still did not include every WGP route used by the app. In particular, `wan_2_2_t2i`, `image_inpaint`, and `annotated_image_edit` had not been exercised in the live RunPod matrix.\n+- This was a validation-plan gap rather than a worker runtime failure.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Post-chain review/sense-check. The chain had completed, but the initial live matrix did not yet map every app-used WGP route into a production-shaped live fixture.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Added live matrix cases for the missing routes.\n+- Reran on pod `wqt0lar8iiyna2`; report `reigh-worker/scripts/live_test/runs/20260507T050214Z/report.md` passed `3/3`.\n+- Evidence:\n+  - `wan_2_2_t2i`: task `1b4f88de-bcd4-4a85-aaad-3e55ce8d5e85`, generation `d3cd6ec7-1075-4f91-ac4c-30735f834b3a`.\n+  - `image_inpaint`: task `533ea421-c27a-4852-a535-0908085f59ad`, generation `dbb46ba6-fca2-4f58-b2bd-a0f70affde8b`.\n+  - `annotated_image_edit`: task `cb727db9-7b6e-4665-b702-25c0d4518ad9`, generation `e91a4e2b-2594-498f-b3fc-16f2a2319ba0`.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- \"Every endpoint\" needs a concrete route ledger before live validation starts. A matrix that is representative is not enough when the user is asking for 1.2GP/WGP parity evidence.\n+\n+### Qwen URL Fields Produced Noisy WGP Input Warnings\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- `image_inpaint` and `annotated_image_edit` completed, but the worker emitted warnings about URL-style image inputs after the handler had already materialized those images into local/generated input fields.\n+- The warnings were nonfatal, but they made a clean live proof look suspicious and could hide real warnings later.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Reigh Worker Qwen handler input normalization during live WGP direct-route runs.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Patched `source/models/model_handlers/qwen_handler.py` to clear raw URL/image fields after materializing them into the internal `image_guide`, inpaint composite, annotated composite, or style-reference fields.\n+- Added regression tests in `tests/test_qwen_model_selection.py`.\n+- Reran the affected routes in the expanded live matrix; `qwen_image_edit`, `image_inpaint`, and `annotated_image_edit` all completed on pod `xhgccre7prd1sj`.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- A route adapter should leave the downstream model handler with one canonical representation of each image input. Keeping both raw URL fields and materialized fields creates misleading diagnostics.\n+\n+### Fresh RunPod Heartbeat Was Not The Same As Worker Readiness\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- The live harness waited for a fresh worker heartbeat and then inserted queue tasks.\n+- On fresh pods, the worker can heartbeat before heavyweight WGP import and queue startup are complete. That starts the test timeout early and can make a healthy pod look unavailable.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Reigh Worker `scripts/live_test/heartbeat_waiter.py`, during fresh WGP RunPod validation.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Patched the live waiter to require both a fresh heartbeat and `metadata.ready_for_tasks == true` for several dwell polls before inserting tasks.\n+- The focused join/edit rerun on pod `3u5zwyqmx167fl` proved the fix: heartbeat became fresh first, readiness stayed false while WGP imported, then `worker ready for tasks` was logged after readiness became true.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Heartbeat should mean \"process alive\"; readiness should mean \"safe to enqueue real work.\" The live harness needs both signals and should expose them separately in progress logs.\n+\n+### Join/Edit Orchestrators Exposed A Real Worker Bug\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- The expanded WGP matrix passed five routes but failed both `join_clips_orchestrator` and `edit_video_orchestrator`.\n+- Child task inspection showed the root error was `local variable 'max_safe_blend' referenced before assignment`.\n+- This was not a RunPod availability quirk and not a Megaplan harness issue. It was a genuine Reigh Worker join-generation edge case: when VACE returned more transition frames than expected, the mismatch branch could reference `max_safe_blend` before initialization.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Reigh Worker `source/task_handlers/join/generation.py`, during the expanded live WGP matrix on pod `xhgccre7prd1sj`.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Initialized `max_safe_blend = context_frame_count` before the transition-frame mismatch branch.\n+- Added/ran focused regression coverage with the live harness and join tests:\n+  `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m pytest tests/test_join_orchestrator_and_registry.py scripts/live_test/tests/test_primitives.py tests/test_qwen_model_selection.py -q`\n+  returned `80 passed, 2 warnings`.\n+- Reran the failing live cases on fresh pod `3u5zwyqmx167fl`; report `reigh-worker/scripts/live_test/runs/20260507T062420Z/report.md` passed `2/2`.\n+- Evidence:\n+  - `join_clips_orchestrator`: task `1e8f67e8-4396-4502-add2-a6fcda931342`, generation `d18b8244-9017-4957-8fe1-ef6a3b7f7861`, output MP4.\n+  - `edit_video_orchestrator`: task `ae0e7523-8d9f-463f-8e2d-191de393ccdd`, generation `494b8dd2-188d-4461-a8f2-a317d1e30707`, output MP4.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- The user's instruction to test real RunPod paths was important. Local contract tests would not have exposed this VACE transition-frame edge case.\n+- When a live route fails, first classify it by layer: harness false negative, infrastructure availability, adapter contract mismatch, or real worker runtime bug. The fix path differs for each layer.\n+\n+### Fresh WGP Installs Are A UX Problem Even When Correct\n+\n+What happened:\n+\n+- Fresh WGP pods commonly spent about five minutes installing the worker environment and another several minutes importing WGP before queue readiness.\n+- This was legitimate startup work, not a failure, but it made live validation feel stalled and amplified the impact of weak progress logs.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- RunPod fresh validation lifecycle and Reigh Worker startup.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- The harness should make long startup phases visible with explicit install/import/readiness progress.\n+- Productively improving this means caching or image prebuild work in the RunPod template path, not only longer timeouts.\n*** End Patch\n"
```
```json
}
```

`annotated_image_edit` -> `edit/qwen_image_edit`\n+- Added adapter scratchpad generation for Qwen 2512/edit, per-run Comfy\n+  input/output/temp directories, image input materialization, and mask/annotation\n+  composite generation for the edit-family routes.\n+- Local validation:\n+  `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m pytest scripts/live_test/tests/test_primitives.py tests/test_vibecomfy_adapter.py tests/test_template_routing.py tests/test_vibecomfy_backend_selection.py -q`\n+  returned `157 passed, 2 warnings`.\n+- Live validation:\n+  `reigh-worker/scripts/live_test/runs/20260507T065745Z/report.md`, pod\n+  `v7ozyfck7hqhbb`, `5/5 passed`.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Route promotion needs two checks: whether a matching VibeComfy template exists,\n+  and whether the Reigh Worker adapter can translate the production payload into\n+  that template's expected inputs.\n+- Do not demote an available route just because the chain did not wire it.\n+  Conversely, do not promote by name similarity: plain `qwen_image` remains\n+  WGP-only because aliasing it to `qwen_image_2512` would change model behavior.\n+\n+### Remaining VibeComfy Gaps Are Template/Parity Gaps, Not RunPod Flakiness\n+\n+What I checked:\n+\n+- VibeComfy source contains no `ready_templates/video/wanvideo_wrapper_22_14b_vace_cocktail.py`.\n+- VibeComfy has Z-Image text-to-image and Flux edit templates, but no proven\n+  `z_image_turbo_i2i` parity template.\n+- VibeComfy has Wan 2.1/2.2 video wrappers, but no proven template matching the\n+  production `wan_2_2_t2i` single-frame image contract.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- These routes should remain WGP-only/fail-closed until real templates exist and\n+  pass the same selected-template, worker queue, completion, and rollback proof.\n+- The correct next work is template creation/parity validation in VibeComfy for\n+  the missing model contracts, not another retry of the same RunPod matrix.\n*** End Patch\n"

```json
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /tmp/banodoco-hivemind/hivemind/SKILL.md\n@@\n ## Query patterns (PostgREST)\n \n Always URL-encode spaces (`%20`). Use `Accept: application/json` implicitly.\n+Prefer `curl --get --data-urlencode` for anything with parentheses, spaces, or\n+multiple filters; hand-built URLs are easy to get subtly wrong.\n@@\n ### 2. Restrict to high-signal channels\n \n ```bash\n &channel_name=in.(daily_summaries,wan_comfyui,wan_chatter,wan_gens,resources,wan_resources)\n ```\n+\n+For first-pass research, use `daily_summaries` as a narrow equality filter\n+before broadening. It is faster and usually more useful than a wide OR across\n+all channels:\n+\n+```bash\n+curl -sG \"https://[REDACTED]/rest/v1/message_feed\" \\\n+  -H \"[REDACTED] \\\n+  --data-urlencode \"select=content,author_name,channel_name,created_at\" \\\n+  --data-urlencode \"channel_name=eq.daily_summaries\" \\\n+  --data-urlencode \"content=ilike.*VACE*\" \\\n+  --data-urlencode \"order=created_at.desc\" \\\n+  --data-urlencode \"limit=10\"\n+```\n@@\n ## What does NOT work\n \n - **`fts` / full-text search** (`content=fts.foo`) — **times out** on this table.\n   Stick with `ilike`.\n+- Very broad `or=(...)` searches across all channels can also time out,\n+  especially with many spelling variants. If this happens, narrow first by\n+  `channel_name=eq.daily_summaries`, use one or two `content=ilike.*term*`\n+  filters, and only then widen to topic channels.\n - `reactions` is mostly `null` — you can't rank by popularity.\n*** End Patch\n"
```
```json
}
```

> DEVELOPER

Are we missing table database indexes or something? Or is there some more, is there some fundamentally bad thing we're doing in the database or something that's making them slow? There are some of the names that are there on top of it that makes them faster?

> AGENT

Yes, this looks much more like a database/search-indexing problem than an agent-docs problem. The docs fix helps agents avoid the slow path, but the underlying table is probably missing the right indexes for the way we search it.

> AGENT

For Hivemind specifically, the slow queries are likely because we’re doing `ilike.*term*` over `content`.

A normal Postgres btree index will not help much with leading-wildcard searches like:

```sql
content ILIKE '%VACE%'
```

That usually needs one of these:

```sql
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY message_feed_content_trgm_idx
ON message_feed USING gin (content gin_trgm_ops);
```

Also useful:

```sql
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY message_feed_channel_created_idx
ON message_feed (channel_name, created_at DESC);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY message_feed_author_created_idx
ON message_feed (author_name, created_at DESC);
```

If we want proper full-text search instead of substring search, we should add a generated/search column and GIN index:

```sql
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY message_feed_content_fts_idx
ON message_feed USING gin (to_tsvector('english', content));
```

Then query with `fts`/`plfts` only after confirming PostgREST uses that expression/index cleanly.

So: not fundamentally bad to expose this via PostgREST, but broad all-channel substring search without trigram/full-text indexes will be slow. The UX fix is: add trigram + channel/date indexes, keep queries channel-scoped by default, and avoid huge `or=(content.ilike...)` searches unless the DB has the trigram index.

> AGENT

The over-capacity reason now looks systemic: spawn-takeover creates a new worker in the production pool while another warm production worker already satisfies desired capacity. Because the live harness does not queue test tasks until after readiness, the orchestrator sees `2 > 1` and kills the new pod before the matrix can start. That is a harness ordering/coordination bug, not a template bug.

> AGENT

The pod was still killed by orchestrator scale-down, but now after it heartbeated as `active`: `scale_down_idle (capacity 2 > desired 1)`. So inactive registration prevented setup takeover, but once the live worker heartbeats into the production `gpu-vibecomfy-production` pool with no queued tasks, the orchestrator considers it excess and terminates it before the matrix queues tasks. I’m fixing fresh mode to queue tasks before readiness or use an isolated selector namespace so the live pod does not compete with production capacity.

The production orchestrator still sees the fresh worker as idle excess once it heartbeats, because the live-test tasks are queued only after readiness. The minimal durable fix is to queue all matrix tasks before the worker launches, then poll them after readiness. That gives the orchestrator and worker real queued work during startup instead of an apparently idle extra GPU.

> DEVELOPER

And why do we keep having to launch machines? Why don't we just keep the one machine open or are we fixing things with the machine and then relaunching it? Why do we have to keep on relaunching them?

> AGENT

We kept relaunching because each failed attempt was losing the pod before it reached usable task execution, for different harness-level reasons:

- `update --spawn-takeover` pods were being killed by production capacity logic before work was queued. I fixed several harness bugs there, but that path is inherently competing with the orchestrator.
- `fresh` initially registered the pod in a way that let the production orchestrator take it over or scale it down. I patched that, then patched the matrix to queue tasks before readiness so the pod is not seen as idle capacity.
- A couple of pods were already gone by the time cleanup ran (`pod not found`), so there was no machine to keep open.
- The current pod `os1fxg41d4rz9o` is still open and installing; I am not relaunching it while it is alive.

So: no, we should not keep relaunching once we have a viable machine. The repeated launches were caused by harness ownership bugs and orchestrator scale-down killing the live-test pod. The current direction is to make the harness keep one fresh pod alive by registering it safely, queuing work before readiness, and then running the whole matrix on that same pod.

Why is there such a thing as WGP only defaults? Everything should work with vibe comfy.

> DEVELOPER

Or is that something in our lists to work on?

> AGENT

“WGP-only” is not meant to be a permanent product default. It is the current route-contract label for workflows that have not yet been adapted to VibeComfy parity, so the live VibeComfy harness should not block direct supported-route validation behind those routes.

Those WGP-only cases are absolutely still on the work list. The filter I just added is a harness correctness fix: it prevents a VibeComfy smoke/parity run from falsely failing on routes we have not yet ported. The broader goal remains to replace those labels by adapting templates/workflows until the production list has parity.

> AGENT

The worker was terminated by the production orchestrator with `scale_down_idle (capacity 2 > desired 1)`, even though the live task was in progress. That is a real orchestration bug for live-test pods: once the worker heartbeats as active, production scale-down can still reclaim it because the running task is not associated via `worker_id`. Also, my new fail-fast only treated `error` as fatal, not `terminated`; I’m patching that now and then I’ll fix the orchestration exclusion path so live pods are not managed as production capacity.

> TOOL

tool_use apply_patch

```json
{
```
```json
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-worker-orchestrator/gpu_orchestrator/live_test_workers.py\n+\"\"\"Helpers for keeping live-test workers out of production control actions.\"\"\"\n+\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n+from typing import Any, Mapping\n+\n+\n+def is_live_test_worker(worker: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool:\n+    \"\"\"Return True when a worker row is owned by the live-test harness.\"\"\"\n+    metadata = worker.get(\"metadata\")\n+    if not isinstance(metadata, Mapping):\n+        return False\n+\n+    return bool(\n+        metadata.get(\"live_test_variant\")\n+        or metadata.get(\"live_test_run_id\")\n+        or metadata.get(\"live_test\") is True\n+    )\n+\n+\n+def filter_live_test_workers(workers: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:\n+    \"\"\"Workers managed by production orchestration, excluding harness-owned rows.\"\"\"\n+    return [worker for worker in workers if not is_live_test_worker(worker)]\n*** End Patch\n"
}
```

It\n+  never ran `vibecomfy nodes restore`, so `/workspace/vibecomfy/custom_nodes`\n+  did not exist.\n+- This was not RunPod availability. It was a live-harness provisioning bug.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Reigh Worker live-test harness, `scripts/live_test/ssh_bootstrap.py`, during\n+  `clone_install_vibecomfy`.\n+- VibeComfy custom-node install/restore layer, where `restore_pack` cloned\n+  locked repositories but did not reinstall catalogued pip dependencies for\n+  known node packs.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Reigh Worker commit `e8558cc6` now runs\n+  `python3.11 -m vibecomfy.cli nodes restore --lockfile custom_nodes.lock`\n+  during VibeComfy pod bootstrap.\n+- VibeComfy commit `14532c3` now:\n+  - installs known node-pack pip dependencies during lockfile restore;\n+  - expands the WanVideoWrapper class catalog for Wan 2.2 T2I and VACE classes;\n+  - treats core Comfy classes such as `LoadImage` and `SaveImage` as built-ins\n+    for install-plan purposes;\n+  - switches the Wan 2.2 T2I and VACE cocktail templates from explicit\n+    `LoadWanVideoT5TextEncoder` plus `WanVideoTextEncode` to\n+    `WanVideoTextEncodeCached`, matching the Kijai template family more closely.\n+- Local validation:\n+  - Reigh Worker: `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m pytest scripts/live_test/tests/test_primitives.py -q`\n+    returned `59 passed`.\n+  - VibeComfy:\n+    `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m pytest tests/test_nodes_install.py tests/test_ready_templates.py tests/test_model_assets.py tests/test_cli_loader.py -q`\n+    returned `58 passed`.\n+  - VibeComfy template validation:\n+    `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m vibecomfy.cli validate ready_templates/video/wanvideo_wrapper_22_14b_t2i.py`\n+    and the VACE cocktail equivalent both returned `ok`.\n+  - `vibecomfy nodes install-plan` now reports no unresolved classes for both\n+    Wan 2.2 T2I and VACE cocktail.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- A ready-template dependency declaration is not enough. Every live bootstrap\n+  path that claims to run VibeComfy must either restore `custom_nodes.lock` or\n+  explicitly prove no template in the selected matrix needs custom nodes.\n+- Install-plan output should be clean before live proof. Unresolved custom\n+  classes hide real template-porting mistakes and waste paid GPU cycles.\n+- Prefer upstream custom-node graph idioms when adapting templates. In this\n+  case, `WanVideoTextEncodeCached` removed a fragile graph-level T5 loader and\n+  better matched Kijai's WanVideoWrapper examples.\n+\n+### Production Service-Role Claims And PAT Live Claims Differ In Worker Ownership\n+\n+What I checked:\n+\n+- The service-role claim function in\n+  `supabase/migrations/20260506113000_update_claim_next_task_route_selector.sql`\n+  sets `tasks.worker_id = p_worker_id` when claiming queued tasks.\n+- The PAT live-test edge path calls `claim_next_task_user_pat` with only\n+  `p_user_id` and `p_include_active`, so live-test tasks can complete with\n+  `worker_id = null` even though a worker processed them.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Null `worker_id` in the current PAT live-test reports is an observability and\n+  recovery limitation of the validation path, not proof that production\n+  service-role claims lose worker ownership.\n+- It is still worth improving. The live harness creates a worker row and sends\n+  `worker_id`; the PAT claim path should preserve it where possible so live\n+  reports, crash recovery, and debugging match production more closely.\n+\n+### Fresh Live Harness Progress Is Still Too Quiet During Dependency Installs\n+\n+What happened:\n+\n+- On pod `mdbnpqvkz3qkk8`, worker clone took about 118 seconds and worker\n+  install took about 285 seconds before VibeComfy installation began.\n+- During the long install phase, the harness showed the phase timer but no\n+  package-level progress because the remote `uv sync` command is run as one\n+  quiet SSH command.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- The phase-level timers are useful, but not enough for long paid GPU installs.\n+  The next harness improvement should stream or tee install logs and highlight\n+  retry attempts without waiting for the whole remote command to return.\n*** End Patch\n"

The live harness creates a worker row and sends\n-  `worker_id`; the PAT claim path should preserve it where possible so live\n-  reports, crash recovery, and debugging match production more closely.\n+- The VibeComfy live harness should use service-role claim auth when validating\n+  production parity. Reigh Worker commit `cb3463ab` switches fresh VibeComfy\n+  live runs to `WORKER_DB_CLIENT_AUTH_MODE=service` while keeping WGP fresh runs\n+  on PAT auth.\n+\n+### PAT Live Claims Bypassed Route Eligibility And Claimed The Wrong Task\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- The first post-nodepack rerun on pod `mdbnpqvkz3qkk8` reported `0/9 passed`.\n+- Worker preflight passed, VibeComfy startup skipped WGP import correctly, and\n+  the worker became ready. The first claimed task, however, was\n+  `individual_travel_segment`, even though VibeComfy support filtering had put\n+  it at the end of the matrix and the production route gate should only allow\n+  VibeComfy-supported routes.\n+- That task entered the existing WGP travel segment path and invoked Wan2GP\n+  `worker.py` with Reigh worker CLI flags, producing:\n+  `worker.py: error: unrecognized arguments: --supabase-url ... --worker ...`.\n+- The live harness then saw the worker row terminate and marked all queued\n+  cases failed.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Reigh Worker live-test harness authentication mode.\n+- Supabase `claim-next-task` PAT path. The PAT RPC does not receive the\n+  VibeComfy worker backend/profile/selector context that the service-role RPC\n+  receives.\n+\n+Recovery:\n+\n+- Reigh Worker commit `cb3463ab` makes fresh VibeComfy live workers claim with\n+  service-role auth so live parity validation uses the same route-aware claim\n+  function that production VibeComfy workers use.\n+- Local validation:\n+  `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python -m pytest scripts/live_test/tests/test_primitives.py -q`\n+  returned `61 passed`.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- It is not enough for queued fixtures to carry `route_contract`. The claim path\n+  must enforce backend eligibility before execution, otherwise an unsupported\n+  WGP-only task can still be claimed by a VibeComfy worker and crash inside a\n+  legacy path.\n+- Live validation should be production-shaped by default. PAT auth remains\n+  useful for local/user-worker checks, but it is the wrong default for\n+  production VibeComfy backend parity.\n*** End Patch\n"

VibeComfy mode should not\n+  execute imports, warmups, or queue setup that are only meaningful for WGP.\n+- Readiness metadata should mean \"the worker can claim tasks now\", not just\n+  \"preflight passed and a heartbeat guardian is alive\".\n+- The live harness should surface worker log tails or at least status\n+  transitions while polling a long-running task. > DEVELOPER

are we making progress here or going in circles?

> AGENT

We are making progress, but the live run exposed a stacked sequence of real issues rather than one issue.

Concrete progress so far:
- Worker code issue fixed and pushed: VibeComfy workers now reach the task claim loop instead of hanging after preflight.
- Production DB migrations that were missing are now applied.
- Production selector/capability data was missing for VibeComfy routes; I added and applied a migration to seed those.
- Live-test harness bug found and fixed locally: queued spoof tasks only put route metadata inside `params`, but claim SQL requires top-level `tasks.route_key/selected_backend/...`.
- Obsolete claim RPC overload caused PostgREST 500s; I added/applied a migration to remove it and forced schema reload.

Where we are now:
- The first live run was already partially poisoned by the earlier DB/harness bugs. It moved forward once, but the current task is still queued.
- The same pod’s SSH became temporarily unavailable after I tried restarting only the worker process to avoid launching another machine. I’m checking pod state now before deciding whether to reuse it or start a clean run.

So no, not just circles. The path is: fix discovered real blockers, commit/push them, then run a clean VibeComfy matrix with the fixed harness and DB state. The current run is useful as diagnosis, but I do not trust it as final validation because it was queued before the fixes landed.

> AGENT

I’m also cleaning up the dangling SSH probe so we don’t keep adding pressure to the exec-session limit. Next I’m going to commit the harness and DB migration fixes, then run a fresh validation pass rather than treating the contaminated run as proof.

The row is `terminated` while still showing fresh heartbeats and `ready_for_tasks`, so this is not a dead pod. I’m patching update mode to explicitly re-register the worker row for live-test takeover.

```json
{
```
```json
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-worker/scripts/live_test/preflight.py\n@@\n def ensure_user_cloud_generation_enabled(db, user_id: str) -> bool:\n@@\n     db.supabase.table(\"users\").update({\"settings\": settings}).eq(\"id\", user_id).execute()\n     return True\n \n \n+def ensure_live_test_route_selectors(db, selector_namespace: str, route_keys: list[str], *, backend: str) -> int:\n+    \"\"\"Clone production route selectors into an isolated live-test namespace.\"\"\"\n+    unique_route_keys = sorted({route_key for route_key in route_keys if route_key})\n+    if backend != \"vibecomfy\" or selector_namespace == \"production\" or not unique_route_keys:\n+        return 0\n+\n+    existing = (\n+        db.supabase.table(\"route_backend_selectors\")\n+        .select(\"route_key\")\n+        .eq(\"selector_namespace\", selector_namespace)\n+        .in_(\"route_key\", unique_route_keys)\n+        .execute()\n+    )\n+    existing_keys = {str(row.get(\"route_key\")) for row in _coerce_rows(existing) if row.get(\"route_key\")}\n+    missing_keys = [route_key for route_key in unique_route_keys if route_key not in existing_keys]\n+    if not missing_keys:\n+        return 0\n+\n+    production = (\n+        db.supabase.table(\"route_backend_selectors\")\n+        .select(\"route_key, selected_backend, selector_version, enabled, expires_at, min_worker_version, reason, metadata\")\n+        .eq(\"selector_namespace\", \"production\")\n+        .in_(\"route_key\", missing_keys)\n+        .execute()\n+    )\n+    production_by_key = {str(row.get(\"route_key\")): row for row in _coerce_rows(production) if row.get(\"route_key\")}\n+    still_missing = [route_key for route_key in missing_keys if route_key not in production_by_key]\n+    if still_missing:\n+        raise RuntimeError(\n+            \"Cannot isolate live-test selector namespace; production route selectors are missing for: \"\n+            + \", \".join(still_missing)\n+        )\n+\n+    created = 0\n+    for route_key in missing_keys:\n+        source = production_by_key[route_key]\n+        metadata = source.get(\"metadata\") if isinstance(source.get(\"metadata\"), dict) else {}\n+        payload = {\n+            \"selector_namespace\": selector_namespace,\n+            \"route_key\": route_key,\n+            \"selected_backend\": source.get(\"selected_backend\") or backend,\n+            \"selector_version\": source.get(\"selector_version\") or 1,\n+            \"enabled\": source.get(\"enabled\") is not False,\n+            \"expires_at\": source.get(\"expires_at\"),\n+            \"min_worker_version\": source.get(\"min_worker_version\"),\n+            \"reason\": f\"live-test isolation cloned from production for {route_key}\",\n+            \"metadata\": {\n+                **metadata,\n+                \"live_test\": True,\n+                \"source_selector_namespace\": \"production\",\n+            },\n+        }\n+        db.supabase.table(\"route_backend_selectors\").insert(payload).execute()\n+        created += 1\n+    return created\n+\n+\n def get_or_create_live_test_project(db, user_id: str) -> str:\n*** End Patch\n"
```

> AGENT

This looks like a real VibeComfy integration gap, not just a bad template: the worker runs `vibecomfy run --ensure-packs`, but VibeComfy currently does not ensure declared `model_assets` at run time. That lets templates pass locally when a model happens to be staged and fail in production when one asset is missing. I’m going to add a general `--ensure-models` path in VibeComfy, make the worker use it, and normalize `directory`/`subdir` so authored templates and fetched models behave consistently.

VibeComfy mode should not\n   execute imports, warmups, or queue setup that are only meaningful for WGP.\n - Readiness metadata should mean \"the worker can claim tasks now\", not just\n   \"preflight passed and a heartbeat guardian is alive\".\n - The live harness should surface worker log tails or at least status\n   transitions while polling a long-running task. A queued task plus idle GPU\n   would have made this failure obvious much earlier.\n+\n+## Post-Chain VibeComfy Parity Repair: Qwen And VACE Route Promotion\n+\n+After the chain finished, the sense-check showed a real parity gap: several\n+routes that the app can select were still treated as WGP-only, while the chain\n+had only proven a narrower ready-template surface. The post-chain repair focused\n+on proving and promoting only routes that could pass through the real Reigh\n+worker, live RunPod, VibeComfy, Supabase task completion, and uploaded artifact\n+path.\n+\n+Final live proof:\n+\n+- `reigh-worker/scripts/live_test/runs/20260507T223010Z/report.md`:\n+  `6/6 passed` for direct image/Qwen/edit cases on pod `uem4ds6heuwu83`.\n+- `reigh-worker/scripts/live_test/runs/20260507T232825Z/report.md`:\n+  `qwen_image_t2i` passed through the promoted base `qwen_image` route.\n+- `reigh-worker/scripts/live_test/runs/20260507T235320Z/report.md`:\n+  `3/3 passed` for individual VACE flow/canny/depth after memory fixes.\n+- `reigh-worker/scripts/live_test/runs/20260508T003727Z/report.md`:\n+  `4/4 passed` for VACE raw/flow/canny/depth `travel_segment` video-source\n+  route keys.\n+\n+Production publication:\n+\n+- VibeComfy PR #7 contains the WanVideo/VACE template, model asset, and memory\n+  profile fixes.\n+- Reigh Worker PR #31 contains route mapping, VibeComfy scratchpad, live matrix,\n+  and preflight fixes.\n+- Reigh App branch\n+  `megaplan/vibecomfy-sprint-09-control-rail-travel-matrix` now contains and\n+  has deployed migration\n+  `20260508003000_seed_vibecomfy_vace_mode_and_qwen_routes.sql`.\n+\n+### `qwen_image` Was A Route Inventory Gap, Not A Template Gap\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- The app uses `qwen_image` as a base route, but the VibeComfy implementation\n+  only had explicit ready-template support for `qwen_image_2512` and related\n+  edit/style routes.\n+- That created a misleading \"WGP-only defaults\" situation: the real capability\n+  existed, but the production route key did not map to it.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Route inventory and selector planning. The initial plan copied ready-template\n+  names instead of checking every app-used route key against the worker route\n+  resolver.\n+\n+Fix:\n+\n+- Promoted `qwen_image` to VibeComfy by mapping it to template\n+  `image/qwen_image_2512` in the worker.\n+- Added live matrix coverage and production selector/capability seed rows.\n+- Proved it with task `9f15c9ed-59a4-4b99-a311-0b5ba654fbfc`, generation\n+  `7fafb706-2876-43d9-80aa-e464539a6fc0`.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Parity work must inventory canonical app route keys, not just available\n+  template filenames. A template can be correct and still fail parity if the app\n+  route key does not resolve to it.\n+\n+### VACE Mode Coverage Needed Real Worker Contracts, Not Template Copies\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- VACE raw/flow/canny/depth and video-source continuity were not all represented\n+  in `template_routing.py`.\n+- The first added live fixtures for `travel_segment` video-source routes failed\n+  before reaching VibeComfy because they did not include the full orchestrator\n+  child contract: `base_prompts_expanded`, `negative_prompts_expanded`,\n+  `segment_frames_expanded`, `num_new_segments_to_generate`, and\n+  `frame_overlap_expanded`.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Execution/live-test fixture design. The fixture looked like a route selector\n+  test, not a production-shaped child task.\n+\n+Fix:\n+\n+- Added VACE route keys for individual travel segment flow/canny/depth and\n+  travel segment raw/flow/canny/depth video-source continuity.\n+- Updated live fixtures to include production-shaped `orchestrator_details`,\n+  `continuation_config`, image inputs, video source inputs, guidance settings,\n+  prompt expansion, frame counts, overlap, seed, and FPS helpers.\n+- Proved all four video-source variants live:\n+  `b6e9b912-aea4-4533-932f-b90a351a0aed`,\n+  `7acae1fa-34c3-44c0-955b-4690385829db`,\n+  `78d4d45c-523e-4f68-9a2a-69fecd4af230`, and\n+  `e9c27fc7-9ecb-483b-9763-37bdf2e4e32f`.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Live fixtures must be production-shaped at the task payload level. A route key\n+  alone is not enough for orchestrator child routes, because the worker code\n+  depends on expanded child-task metadata before it can even build the\n+  VibeComfy scratchpad.\n+\n+### VACE OOM Was A Real Runtime Profile Bug\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- VACE flow/canny/depth initially failed on the 24GB 4090 pod with real CUDA\n+  out-of-memory errors. This was not RunPod availability noise.\n+- The failure recommended `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`,\n+  and the VACE workflow also needed more aggressive block swapping/offload for\n+  this hardware class.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- VibeComfy runtime profile and Reigh Worker scratchpad generation.\n+\n+Fix:\n+\n+- Set `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` for VibeComfy\n+  subprocess execution.\n+- Updated VACE WanVideo defaults to use safer block swapping and offload\n+  settings.\n+- Re-ran individual VACE flow/canny/depth live and got `3/3 passed`.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Memory profile is part of parity. A workflow that only runs on a large or\n+  unusually clean GPU is not production-ready for the current RunPod fleet.\n+\n+### Selector Fallback Was Not Enough Without Capabilities\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- During branch-only route testing, the live harness could synthesize selector\n+  rows, but claim eligibility still needed matching `route_backend_capabilities`\n+  rows.\n+- Without both rows, a test could be present in the route map but invisible or\n+  ineligible to the production-shaped claim path.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Live-test preflight/harness, not VibeComfy itself.\n+\n+Fix:\n+\n+- The live-test preflight now synthesizes isolated selector rows and\n+  live-test-only backend capability rows for branch-only routes.\n+- Production promotion then added durable app migrations only after the live\n+  proof passed.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Selector and capability metadata are a pair. Future route promotion should\n+  require both local branch synthesis for testing and a production migration for\n+  durable rollout.\n+\n+### Pod Reuse Was Correct, But The Harness Still Needs A Pod Lock\n+\n+What happened:\n+\n+- The successful post-chain proof reused pod `uem4ds6heuwu83` rather than\n+  relaunching repeatedly.\n+- Earlier overlapping live runs left stale worker processes and could terminate\n+  a generation when a new run took over the same pod.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Live-test orchestration and cleanup ergonomics.\n+\n+Fix made during this run:\n+\n+- Stale worker-process cleanup was hardened, and the operator stopped launching\n+  overlapping live matrices on the same pod.\n+\n+Remaining harness improvement:\n+\n+- Add an explicit pod-level live-test lock or takeover guard. Reusing one pod is\n+  the right default for expensive GPU validation, but concurrent runs against\n+  the same pod should fail fast or require an explicit takeover flag.\n+\n+### Production Selector Namespace Was A Database Contract Issue\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- Claiming tasks by backend/profile can go wrong if queued tasks from another\n+  selector namespace remain visible to a VibeComfy worker.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Supabase `claim_next_task_service_role` and related task count RPCs.\n+\n+Fix:\n+\n+- Reigh App migration\n+  `20260507215500_respect_task_selector_namespace_in_claims.sql` filters queued\n+  tasks to the effective selector namespace and mirrors that filter in count\n+  RPCs.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Selector namespace is part of the worker claim contract. It must be enforced\n+  in the database, not only in app-side route metadata.\n+\n+### Residual UX Issues\n+\n+- The live worker still logs a duplicate worker-row warning when reusing an\n+  existing pod row and then recovers by patching/reactivating the row. This is\n+  tolerable but noisy.\n+- Successful runs may show SIGTERM/teardown diagnostics after the task has\n+  already completed and uploaded output. The report is the source of truth, but\n+  teardown logging should be clearer.\n+- Long VACE runs mostly show Supabase polling in the local terminal. The harness\n+  should expose periodic worker-log summaries, GPU memory, and current Comfy\n+  node progress so a real hang is distinguishable from a long generation.\n*** End Patch\n"
```json
}
```

```json
{
```
```json
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/learnings/megaplan-vibecomfy-sprint-00a-2026-05-05.md\n@@\n ### Residual UX Issues\n \n - The live worker still logs a duplicate worker-row warning when reusing an\n   existing pod row and then recovers by patching/reactivating the row. This is\n   tolerable but noisy.\n - Successful runs may show SIGTERM/teardown diagnostics after the task has\n   already completed and uploaded output. The report is the source of truth, but\n   teardown logging should be clearer.\n - Long VACE runs mostly show Supabase polling in the local terminal. The harness\n   should expose periodic worker-log summaries, GPU memory, and current Comfy\n   node progress so a real hang is distinguishable from a long generation.\n+\n+### Join VACE Was Advertised But Not Dispatched Through VibeComfy\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- The app/DB/route maps claimed the Wan 2.2 VACE `join_clips_segment`\n+  join-bridge route was VibeComfy-capable, and the VibeComfy adapter could\n+  build the WanVideo VACE scratchpad for it.\n+- The worker runtime still had an explicit `join_clips_segment` handler that\n+  sent the task directly to the legacy join handler. That meant route metadata\n+  and runtime behavior diverged: production could select VibeComfy, but the\n+  actual handler path would not necessarily enter VibeComfy.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Execution/dispatch layer, specifically the worker `TaskRegistry` special\n+  handler path. This was not a template issue and not an app seed issue.\n+\n+Fix:\n+\n+- `join_clips_segment` now resolves its route before dispatch. If the resolved\n+  backend is VibeComfy, it calls the shared resolved-task executor and refuses\n+  to build a WGP task. If the resolved backend is WGP/default, it preserves the\n+  legacy join handler.\n+- Added regression tests proving the VibeComfy VACE join route bypasses the\n+  legacy join handler and the default WGP route still uses it.\n+- Added `join_clips_segment_wan22_vace` to the live matrix and ran it on the\n+  reused pod `uem4ds6heuwu83`: task\n+  `3aecdcbb-0321-4084-81c5-073acf8c235f`, generation\n+  `44fac44b-7018-406d-8d02-065271e06b09`, output\n+  `Wan-2-2-VACE_00001.mp4`, `1/1 passed`.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Route-map parity is insufficient. For every route promoted to VibeComfy,\n+  there must be a handler-dispatch test proving the live worker actually enters\n+  the resolved backend path. Special-case task handlers are a common place for\n+  route metadata to silently stop mattering.\n+\n+### Live-Test Cleanup Missed Absolute `worker.py` Processes\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- Reusing pod `uem4ds6heuwu83` revealed three old `worker.py` processes still\n+  alive after earlier update runs.\n+- The cleanup regex killed `run_worker.py`, `python worker.py`, and\n+  `source.runtime.worker`, but the real live process shape was\n+  `/workspace/.../.venv/bin/python3 -u /workspace/.../worker.py ...`.\n+  That absolute-path form did not match.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Live-test harness cleanup, not RunPod capacity and not VibeComfy.\n+\n+Fix:\n+\n+- Broadened the process scan/kill patterns to match\n+  `python[^ ]* .*worker.py`, covering `python3 -u /absolute/path/worker.py`.\n+- Added a regression test for absolute worker paths and manually cleaned the\n+  live pod. The before scan showed three stale worker processes; the after scan\n+  was empty.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Pod reuse is still the right default, but process cleanup has to match the\n+  exact launched command. Otherwise reuse creates confusing contention and\n+  stale heartbeat/process state that looks like RunPod flakiness.\n*** End Patch\n"
}
```

```json
{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/learnings/megaplan-vibecomfy-sprint-00a-2026-05-05.md\n@@\n ### App-Active Unported Routes Were Implicit, Not Explicit\n@@\n - A production route ledger needs positive and negative contracts. Unsupported\n   active routes should be named explicitly with a blocker/disposition so future\n   promotion work starts from a known state instead of rediscovering gaps.\n+\n+### `wan_2_2_i2v` Was An App Emission And Ownership Mismatch\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- The app travel resolver could emit `task_type: wan_2_2_i2v` when\n+  `turbo_mode: true`.\n+- The Ray worker dispatch catalog does not classify `wan_2_2_i2v` as a direct\n+  queue or WGP-owned task. It would only reach the direct queue through the\n+  generic fallthrough when a queue object exists, and it has no catalog model\n+  mapping.\n+- VibeComfy has a Wan 2.2 5B I2V ready template and Wan 2.1 I2V templates, but\n+  not a proven Wan 2.2 14B Lightning I2V equivalent for the WGP\n+  `wan_2_2_i2v_lightning_baseline_2_2_2` contract. Promoting the available 5B\n+  template would be a model-quality mismatch, not parity.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- App resolver/API contract first, then worker dispatch ownership. This was not\n+  primarily a RunPod capacity issue or a VibeComfy custom-node issue.\n+\n+Fix:\n+\n+- `travelBetweenImagesResolver` now keeps turbo-mode travel requests on the\n+  owned `travel_orchestrator` path until direct Wan I2V has a real runtime\n+  owner, selector seed, and live proof.\n+- Added an app resolver regression test proving `turbo_mode: true` no longer\n+  emits the worker-unowned `wan_2_2_i2v` task type.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- A template candidate is not enough. Direct-route promotion requires matching\n+  model identity, worker dispatch ownership, app emission behavior, selector\n+  metadata, and live proof. If any one of those is missing, keep the request on\n+  the known route and fail closed for VibeComfy.\n*** End Patch\n"
}
```

```json
{
```
```json
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/learnings/megaplan-vibecomfy-sprint-00a-2026-05-05.md\n@@\n Learning:\n \n - A template candidate is not enough. Direct-route promotion requires matching\n   model identity, worker dispatch ownership, app emission behavior, selector\n   metadata, and live proof. If any one of those is missing, keep the request on\n   the known route and fail closed for VibeComfy.\n+\n+### Timeline Agent Route Aliases Could Bypass Resolver Intent\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- The AI timeline agent has two generation surfaces: the newer `create_task`\n+  tool and the older `create_generation_task` helper.\n+- `create_task` emits canonical hyphenated task types such as `image-to-video`,\n+  `image-upscale`, `video-enhance`, and `character-animate`.\n+- `create_generation_task` advertised snake_case aliases such as\n+  `travel_between_images`, `image_upscale`, `video_enhance`, and\n+  `character_animate`, but its route switch only handled the hyphenated names.\n+- A snake_case alias could therefore fall through to the default\n+  `image_generation` request builder instead of reaching the matching\n+  create-task resolver and route selector.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- App-side timeline-agent adapter layer, before the create-task resolver\n+  registry. This was not a VibeComfy runtime bug or RunPod issue; it was an\n+  app translation drift between two supported tool surfaces.\n+\n+Fix:\n+\n+- Updated `supabase/functions/ai-timeline-agent/tools/generation.ts` so\n+  snake_case aliases and hyphenated task types map to the same create-task\n+  families.\n+- Added `supabase/functions/ai-timeline-agent/tools/generation.test.ts` to\n+  prove text-to-image, image-to-video, image-to-image, magic edit,\n+  image upscale, video enhance, and character animate all post the expected\n+  create-task family in both supported naming forms.\n+- Ran the focused regression slice:\n+  `npm run test:edge:unit -- --run supabase/functions/ai-timeline-agent/tools/generation.test.ts supabase/functions/ai-timeline-agent/tools/create-task.test.ts supabase/functions/create-task/resolvers/__tests__/placement.test.ts supabase/functions/create-task/resolvers/shared/routeKeys.test.ts`\n+  (`4 files, 59 tests passed`).\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- App-active route validation must include every adapter that can enqueue a\n+  task, not only the visible UI submit buttons and edge resolver registry.\n+  Legacy aliases need explicit tests because silent fallback to a default\n+  generator looks like \"it queued\" while bypassing the intended route contract.\n*** End Patch\n"
}
```

> DEVELOPER

So absolutely everything is working now?

> AGENT

Not “absolutely everything” in the sense of every possible app feature being ported to VibeComfy.

What is true now:

- The megaplan chain is complete.
- The promoted VibeComfy routes have live RunPod/Reigh-worker proof.
- Every app-active create-task family now has an explicit route state:
  - VibeComfy-supported and live-proven,
  - WGP/API-owned,
  - or VibeComfy-unsupported/fail-closed.
- The app/worker contract tests pass.
- The app PR GitHub check passed.
- Docs and learning log are updated.

What is still not VibeComfy parity:

- `image-upscale`
- `video_enhance`
- `animate_character`
- `flux_klein_edit`
- direct `wan_2_2_i2v`

Those are intentionally not promoted to VibeComfy yet. They are covered by explicit unsupported/fail-closed contracts or preserved on their existing WGP/API owner paths.

So the accurate status is: everything we have promoted or kept active is now accounted for and validated. Complete “everything works on VibeComfy” parity is not done, because some app-active routes remain intentionally non-VibeComfy until they get real templates/runtime ownership/live proof.

> DEVELOPER

Why didn't you do them?

> AGENT

Because they were not “missing wiring” tasks. They need real implementation work before they can honestly be marked VibeComfy-supported.

Specifically:

- `wan_2_2_i2v`: no proven Wan 2.2 14B Lightning I2V VibeComfy template matched the existing WGP contract, and the worker did not actually own `wan_2_2_i2v` as a proper direct route. Promoting the available 5B/2.1 templates would have been fake parity.
- `image-upscale`, `video_enhance`, `animate_character`: these are API/non-RayWorker owned today. They need VibeComfy templates, input/output adapters, route selectors, completion/billing parity, and live RunPod proof before promotion.
- `flux_klein_edit`: similar issue, and it currently has its own model/API contract rather than a proven VibeComfy equivalent.

So I chose the defensible fix: make them explicit fail-closed routes instead of silently pretending they worked. That was the right immediate safety move, but it is not the same as completing full VibeComfy parity.

The real answer is: I didn’t do them because I found they required new template/runtime porting work, not just validation, and I stopped after making the active app surface safe and explicit. If the directive is “full VibeComfy parity for those too,” then the next work is to port and live-test those five route families one by one.

> AGENT

I found a real harness issue: VibeComfy’s UI-to-API fallback ignores `widgets_values` when custom nodes store them as a dict. That drops critical fields like `VHS_LoadVideo.video` and `VHS_VideoCombine.save_output`, so WanAnimate can validate structurally while losing its actual inputs. I’m fixing that first, then the templates can carry the Kijai workflows faithfully.

maps Reigh image-upscale parameters without external API calls.\",\n+    \"runtime_note\": \"This preserves the task contract but is not FlashVSR/RealESRGAN model super-resolution.\",\n+}\n+\n+READY_REQUIREMENTS = {\"models\": [], \"custom_nodes\": []}\n+\n+\n+def build() -> VibeWorkflow:\n+    wf = VibeWorkflow(\n+        READY_METADATA[\"ready_template\"],\n+        WorkflowSource(id=READY_METADATA[\"ready_template\"], path=__file__, source_type=\"ready_template\"),\n+    )\n+    image = _node(wf, \"LoadImage\", \"1\", image=\"image_upscale_input.png\")\n+    upscaled = _node(\n+        wf,\n+        \"ImageScaleBy\",\n+        \"2\",\n+        image=image.out(0),\n+        upscale_method=\"lanczos\",\n+        scale_by=2.0,\n+    )\n+    _node(wf, \"SaveImage\", \"3\", filename_prefix=\"image-upscale\", images=upscaled.out(0))\n+\n+    wf.finalize_metadata()\n+    apply_ready_template_policy(wf, READY_METADATA, source_path=__file__, requirements=READY_REQUIREMENTS)\n+    return wf\n+\n+\n+def _node(wf: VibeWorkflow, class_type: str, _id: str, **kwargs):\n+    builder = wf.node(class_type, **kwargs)\n+    if builder.node.id != _id:\n+        old_id = builder.node.id\n+        node = wf.nodes.pop(old_id)\n+        node.id = _id\n+        wf.nodes[_id] = node\n+        for edge in wf.edges:\n+            if edge.to_node == old_id:\n+                edge.to_node = _id\n+            if edge.from_node == old_id:\n+                edge.from_node = _id\n+    return builder\n*** End Patch\n"

> AGENT

The real bug is in VibeComfy’s model-asset normalizer, not just this one template. It respects `directory` and URL-derived split folders, but ignores explicit `subdir`, so non-split-file HuggingFace assets default to `checkpoints`; that is why the Klein UNET landed in the wrong place despite the template saying `diffusion_models`. I’m fixing that harness edge case with a regression test.

There’s a second harness bug in the same path: VibeComfy compiles `node.inputs` and then overlays `node.widgets`, so scratchpads that set `inputs["widget_0"]` do not actually override the original imported widget value. > AGENT

For `port check`, I’d keep it as orchestration and reporting, not the owner of every fix. The right split is: core workflow compilation owns helper-node behavior; schema/widget utilities own widget-only positional mapping; custom-node registry owns pack inference; asset analysis owns model candidates; `port check` composes those into a preflight report and catches cross-layer mismatches before live validation.

> AGENT

After the analyzer is in place, the next useful abstraction is a converter that consumes the analyzer result and emits either scratchpad Python by default or a ready-template candidate only when explicitly promoted. After that, I’d wire `port check` into the live-test workflow so every production route gets a cheap local preflight before RunPod.

I’d keep the current standard Megaplan as the umbrella and let it execute the first slice unless it fails. For future splits: `port check` deserves standard if done alone because it crosses workflow loading, schema, helpers, packs, assets, CLI, and docs; the converter can be light once `port check` exposes a stable analysis object.

They can overlap only after the analyzer interface is fixed. Before that, concurrent converter work risks guessing the same provenance/schema/helper concepts and creating two competing abstractions. The clean agent role is: run `port check`, read the structured report, fix the specific layer it points at, rerun locally, then only use RunPod when the report is clean or has explicitly accepted warnings.

The code confirms the mismatch: update mode waits for `metadata.ready_for_tasks` before it queues the task, but the worker is already in the claim loop and polling an empty namespace. I’m going to patch the harness so VibeComfy update-mode can treat an active claim loop heartbeat as ready, then queue the case instead of deadlocking on a marker that is not being set.

> DEVELOPER

no/bad process or not adherence? wow do we fix?

> AGENT

This was both a tooling gap and an adherence/process miss.

Tooling gap: `port check` did not compare the final compiled API prompt against required schema inputs. It checked unresolved `widget_N` names and generic validation, but generic validation only sees what the current schema provider knows; in this run the provider was empty/local, so the allowlist mismatch slipped through.

Process miss: after adding schema entries, I accepted “unresolved widgets = 0” as sufficient without inspecting the compiled prompt for the exact required fields on the new custom-node classes. That was too weak for a production RunPod validation path. I’m fixing the tool so the process can’t make that same mistake silently: local port check should report “node has widget values that map to required names, but compiled API is missing those names” before GPU time is spent.

> AGENT

I’m adding the guard at the port workbench level: after compile, it scans positional widget values against committed widget schemas and, when schema data says the named input is required, reports an error if the compiled API lacks that named input. For empty schema environments, it will still flag known custom-node-pack classes, which covers the RunPod gap we just hit without turning every legacy core widget into noise.

> AGENT

For output-artifact contracts, I’d make it a first-class VibeComfy contract rather than a worker convention: every runtime should emit absolute artifact paths resolved from Comfy’s configured `output_directory`, every `run` metadata file should include both `outputs_raw` and `outputs_resolved`, and `port check` should warn when a ready template has save nodes that can’t be mapped to the standard output directory. The worker should keep a fallback resolver, but treat it as compatibility, not the main path.

For pod/run introspection, I’d build a single `live-test inspect` command that takes `--pod-id`, `--worker-id`, or `--task-id` and returns one compact status bundle: RunPod desired/actual status, SSH endpoint, worker DB row, last heartbeat age, active task status, recent worker log tail, VibeComfy run metadata paths, and artifact existence checks. That would replace the manual pattern of jumping between Supabase, SSH, RunPod status, and local reports.

I’d split them differently.

Output-artifact contracts are small enough for a determined subagent or a light megaplan, because the scope is coherent: VibeComfy runtime output normalization, metadata schema, port-check diagnostics, and worker fallback cleanup. Pod/run introspection deserves a standard megaplan or at least a light megaplan with review, because it crosses RunPod lifecycle, worker live-test CLI, Supabase schema/query behavior, SSH log fetching, and report UX. It is only proven\n+  after the worker can create the app-shaped task, claim it, generate the media,\n+  resolve the artifact, enforce the media contract, upload the result, and mark\n+  the task complete.\n+- Required template inputs and duration controls should be machine-checkable.\n+  Missing required connections and unbound output lengths are exactly the kind\n+  of issue a port-check tool should catch before live GPU time.\n+- VibeComfy/worker observability still needs improvement. During the successful\n+  19-minute run, the worker heartbeat showed liveness but `worker.log` did not\n+  expose meaningful per-node Comfy progress. A pod/run introspection tool should\n+  report subprocess status, recent Comfy stdout/stderr, artifact directory\n+  growth, and last modified output files.\n+\n+### RunPod Lifecycle Drift Was A Harness Bug, Not Merely Pod Flakiness\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- Reusing an old pod failed because RunPod status/SSH lookup returned schema\n+  errors and then no usable SSH details.\n+- The lifecycle library queried fields that no longer exist in the current\n+  RunPod GraphQL schema: `Pod.actualStatus` and `PodRuntime.ip`.\n+- The status helper also returned too early after a non-200 GraphQL response\n+  instead of falling back to the smaller status query.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- `runpod-lifecycle/src/runpod_lifecycle/api.py`.\n+\n+Fix:\n+\n+- Removed schema-invalid GraphQL fields from the pod status query.\n+- Derived the pod IP from the port mapping data that the schema still exposes.\n+- Retried the minimal status query after a GraphQL HTTP error instead of\n+  stopping early.\n+- Added regression tests covering schema-safe status queries, IP derivation, and\n+  fallback behavior.\n+\n+Validation:\n+\n+- `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/test_api.py tests/test_ssh_details.py -q`\n+  - Result: `14 passed`.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Treat cloud provider API schema drift as a harness reliability issue. It\n+  should be fixed in the shared lifecycle tool instead of worked around per\n+  route.\n+- When a pod cannot be reused, the inspection tool should clearly distinguish\n+  stale/deleted pod, SSH-not-ready, schema/API failure, and worker-not-running.\n+\n+### Live-Test Update Branches Can Hide Useful Commits On Scratch Branches\n+\n+What went wrong:\n+\n+- The live-test update flow mutates the active worker checkout to create\n+  temporary update branches. A sub-agent improvement landed on one of those\n+  temporary branches first, then had to be cherry-picked back onto the intended\n+  sprint branch.\n+\n+Where it happened:\n+\n+- Live-test update harness branch management.\n+\n+Fix this time:\n+\n+- Cherry-picked the useful inspect command onto the intended worker branch and\n+  pushed it.\n+\n+Future fix:\n+\n+- Run update-variant live tests from a disposable worktree or clone, not the\n+  developer's active repo checkout.\n+- If the harness must change branches, it should restore the original branch\n+  and print a loud warning when it cannot.\n+\n+Learning:\n+\n+- Live tests are implementation tools, but they should not make the source\n+  checkout harder to reason about. Branch mutation is acceptable only when it\n+  is explicit, isolated, and recoverable.\n*** End Patch\n"
```json
}
```

> DEVELOPER

Is there some kind of deeper reasons these fixes like a missing abstraction or a missing tool or is it just stuff that we need to patch up to get it working? Like are we getting to the root of the issue basically?

> AGENT

Yes, there are deeper reasons. This was not just a pile of one-off bugs.

The main missing abstractions are:

1. **Workflow port contract**
   We need a first-class way to say: this Reigh task param maps to this Comfy node input, this media input maps here, this output must be produced here, this frame count/fps/resolution must match. Right now too much of that lives in ad hoc scratchpad code and human inspection.

2. **Required connection / required input validator**
   The `PointsEditor` and frame-length issues should have been caught before live RunPod. VibeComfy should validate required Comfy/custom-node inputs, unbound template controls, output nodes, and artifact paths before burning GPU time.

3. **Output artifact contract**
   The `output/Wanimate_00001_.mp4` issue showed that VibeComfy and the worker did not share a strong artifact contract. We’ve improved this, but the real abstraction is: every workflow declares expected output type, save node, output directory, filename discovery strategy, and media validation requirements.

4. **Route parity manifest**
   We need one source of truth per route: WGP behavior, VibeComfy template, app params, worker params, expected outputs, live proof status, and known non-parities. The docs now approximate this, but it should be machine-readable and testable.

5. **Run/pod introspection**
   We had heartbeats but weak Comfy progress visibility. The inspect command helps, but the deeper missing tool is a proper “what is this live generation doing?” view: process state, Comfy stdout/stderr, active node, artifact directory growth, recent file mtimes, GPU utilization, and task DB state in one place.

6. **Workflow import/conversion tooling**
   A lot of drag came from adapting UI JSON/custom-node workflows into our Python-esque VibeComfy template format. That should be a toolchain: ingest workflow, preserve dict widgets, infer model assets, identify required nodes, emit a draft Python template, then validate it against Reigh route contracts.

So: the individual fixes were necessary, but the pattern is clear. We are getting closer to the root by turning repeated failure modes into harness/tooling improvements. The next root-level move is to formalize **route/workflow contracts** and make port-check validation enforce them before live execution. That would prevent most of the failures we hit: missing inputs, wrong save path, wrong frame count, wrong model directory, and unclear live state.

> DEVELOPER

And how are we interacting with VibeComfy? Is it a dependancy? A submodule? What makes sense for our relationship with it?

> AGENT

I’ll quickly verify the workspace layout so I can answer this concretely rather than from memory.

> AGENT

VibeComfy is currently a separate sibling repo/package in the workspace, not a normal tracked submodule of the top-level repo.

How `reigh-worker` interacts with it today:
- Worker does **not import VibeComfy directly** in routing code.
- For VibeComfy routes, `reigh-worker` builds scratchpad Python and runs:

```bash
python3.11 -m vibecomfy.cli run <workflow_ref> --runtime embedded --ensure-packs --ensure-models
```

- It finds VibeComfy through `VIBECOMFY_CWD` / `VIBECOMFY_PATH` / `PYTHONPATH`.
- Live RunPod validation clones and installs VibeComfy separately, usually from `megaplan/production-parity-templates`.

What makes sense long term:
- Treat VibeComfy as a **separately versioned runtime/tooling package**, not as copied code inside `reigh-worker`.
- Pin it explicitly in production, ideally by git SHA or release version, so a worker image/run knows exactly which VibeComfy behavior and templates it has.
- Keep the boundary stable: `reigh-worker` owns Reigh task semantics, route selection, WGP parity contracts, uploads/downloads, DB status; VibeComfy owns Comfy workflow IR, template conversion, validation, custom-node/model checks, and execution.
- Avoid making it a git submodule unless we truly want top-level workspace pinning. Submodules add friction, and this workspace already has a broken gitlink-style situation for another path. A pinned package/install ref is cleaner for production.

The weak point right now is that the relationship is too implicit: route support says “VibeComfy supported”, but there is not yet a strong shared contract saying “this template consumes LoRA/control/interpolation/model-selection params.” That is the abstraction I think we need next: a VibeComfy route capability manifest consumed by `reigh-worker` route selection.

```json
{
```
```json
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-worker/source/models/comfy/vibecomfy_adapter.py\n@@\n def _workflow_reference_for_resolved_task(resolved: ResolvedTask, run_workspace: Path) -> tuple[str, bool]:\n@@\n     return str(resolved.template_id), True\n \n \n+def _maybe_postprocess_vibecomfy_output(\n+    *,\n+    resolved: ResolvedTask,\n+    output_path: Path,\n+    run_workspace: Path,\n+) -> Path | None:\n+    if resolved.route_key != \"video_enhance\" or not _bool_param(resolved.params, \"enable_interpolation\"):\n+        return None\n+    interpolation = resolved.params.get(\"interpolation\")\n+    interpolation_params = interpolation if isinstance(interpolation, Mapping) else {}\n+    exp = int(interpolation_params.get(\"exp\") or interpolation_params.get(\"rife_exp\") or 1)\n+    exp = max(1, min(exp, 2))\n+    fps = int(float(resolved.params.get(\"fps\") or 16))\n+    target = run_workspace / \"output\" / f\"video-enhance-rife-x{2 ** exp}.mp4\"\n+    return _rife_interpolate_video(output_path, target, fps=fps, exp=exp)\n+\n+\n+def _rife_interpolate_video(input_path: Path, output_path: Path, *, fps: int, exp: int) -> Path:\n+    import cv2\n+    import numpy as np\n+    import torch\n+\n+    from source.media.video.ffmpeg_ops import create_video_from_frames_list\n+    from source.media.video.frame_extraction import extract_frames_from_video\n+    from source.runtime.wgp_bridge import run_rife_temporal_interpolation\n+\n+    frames_bgr = extract_frames_from_video(input_path)\n+    if len(frames_bgr) < 2:\n+        raise ValueError(f\"RIFE interpolation requires at least two frames, got {len(frames_bgr)} from {input_path}\")\n+\n+    height, width = frames_bgr[0].shape[:2]\n+    frames_rgb = [cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB) for frame in frames_bgr]\n+    sample_np = np.stack(frames_rgb, axis=0).astype(np.float32) / 127.5 - 1.0\n+    sample = torch.from_numpy(sample_np).permute(3, 0, 1, 2)\n+    device = \"cuda\" if torch.cuda.is_available() else \"cpu\"\n+    sample = sample.to(device)\n+\n+    ckpt = _rife_checkpoint_path(prefer_v4=True)\n+    output = run_rife_temporal_interpolation(str(ckpt), sample, exp, device=device)\n+    if output is None:\n+        raise RuntimeError(\"RIFE interpolation returned no frames\")\n+\n+    output = output.to(\"cpu\")\n+    frames_out: list[np.ndarray] = []\n+    for index in range(output.shape[1]):\n+        frame = output[:, index]\n+        frame_rgb = ((frame.permute(1, 2, 0).numpy() + 1.0) * 127.5).clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)\n+        frames_out.append(cv2.cvtColor(frame_rgb, cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR))\n+\n+    output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n+    return create_video_from_frames_list(frames_out, output_path, fps * (2 ** exp), (width, height))\n+\n+\n+def _rife_checkpoint_path(*, prefer_v4: bool) -> Path:\n+    repo_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]\n+    candidates = []\n+    if prefer_v4:\n+        candidates.append(repo_root / \"Wan2GP\" / \"ckpts\" / \"rife4.26.pkl\")\n+    candidates.append(repo_root / \"Wan2GP\" / \"ckpts\" / \"flownet.pkl\")\n+    for candidate in candidates:\n+        if candidate.is_file():\n+            return candidate\n+    raise FileNotFoundError(\n+        \"RIFE checkpoint missing; expected Wan2GP/ckpts/rife4.26.pkl or Wan2GP/ckpts/flownet.pkl\"\n+    )\n+\n+\n def _write_z_image_scratchpad(resolved: ResolvedTask, run_workspace: Path) -> Path:\n*** End Patch\n"
}
```

And should we be creating kind of like scratch pads or whatever we call them on top of Comfy workflows that actually execute this stuff? Or should this logic be held inside of one 2GP or how do you think it should actually be working together? Yeah, I don't know.

> AGENT

For the VibeComfy path, I think the right split is: Comfy/VibeComfy should own graph-native generation and graph-native preprocessing; the worker should own task orchestration, app payload normalization, artifact contracts, uploads, and small postprocessing that is not naturally a Comfy graph. RIFE `video_enhance` sits on the boundary: long-term it would be cleaner as a VibeComfy block/tool if we can package the model reliably, but for parity today the adapter postprocess is better than routing to Wan2GP or pretending the feature is unsupported.

> AGENT

That `72GB` line is almost certainly the RunPod launcher’s **system RAM tier**, not GPU VRAM. It is asking RunPod for a 4090 plus at least 72GB host memory because the live-test/orchestrator defaults are conservative, not because the model needs a 72GB GPU. That can make availability much worse even though the actual workload would fit on a normal 4090 machine.

This points to a real launcher UX issue: the test runner should either default to the same 4090-compatible shape we know production uses, or choose the RAM tier based on the selected cases. I’m going to let this current provision attempt finish or fail, then I’ll inspect the launcher defaults and lower the live-test requirement if it’s just an overbroad default.

This is now clearer: the problem is not total disk capacity, it is the MooseFS `/workspace` quota/flush behavior while `uv` extracts hundreds of packages into `.venv` and cache on the network volume. The right fix is stronger: keep the repo on `/workspace`, but put both the `uv` cache and the project virtualenv on the pod’s 200GB local root disk, then run the worker with the same `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT`.

```json
{
```
```json
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-worker/scripts/live_test/variant_update.py\n@@\n def _extract_worker_id_from_cmdline(cmdline: list[str]) -> str | None:\n     for index, item in enumerate(cmdline):\n         if item == \"--worker\" and index + 1 < len(cmdline):\n             return cmdline[index + 1]\n     return None\n+\n+\n+def _is_retryable_ssh_drop(exc: Exception) -> bool:\n+    message = str(exc).lower()\n+    return (\n+        \"ssh session not active\" in message\n+        or \"exit -1\" in message\n+        or \"socket is closed\" in message\n+        or \"connection reset\" in message\n+        or \"connection lost\" in message\n+        or \"broken pipe\" in message\n+    )\n+\n+\n+def _clone_and_install_vibecomfy_with_reconnect(\n+    ssh,\n+    *,\n+    pod_id: str,\n+    api_key: str,\n+    repo_url: str,\n+    branch: str,\n+    workdir: str,\n+    python_path: str,\n+    attempts: int = 2,\n+):\n+    current_ssh = ssh\n+    for attempt in range(1, attempts + 1):\n+        try:\n+            clone_and_install_vibecomfy(\n+                current_ssh,\n+                repo_url=repo_url,\n+                branch=branch,\n+                workdir=workdir,\n+                python_path=python_path,\n+            )\n+            return current_ssh\n+        except Exception as exc:\n+            if attempt >= attempts or not _is_retryable_ssh_drop(exc):\n+                raise\n+            log.warning(\n+                \"VibeComfy checkout/install lost SSH; reconnecting and retrying\",\n+                attempt=attempt,\n+                attempts=attempts,\n+                pod_id=pod_id,\n+                error=str(exc),\n+            )\n+            disconnect = getattr(current_ssh, \"disconnect\", None)\n+            if callable(disconnect):\n+                try:\n+                    disconnect()\n+                except Exception:\n+                    pass\n+            current_ssh = open_session(pod_id, api_key, ssh_wait_timeout=180)\n+    return current_ssh\n*** End Patch\n"
}
```

> DEVELOPER

Ae we making progress here? What have we been doing lately? What's been taking up our time? Any tools we're missing?

> AGENT

Yes, we’re making real progress, not just circling.

Lately I’ve been doing three things:

1. Live validation on RunPod through the actual worker/VibeComfy path.
   Confirmed live passes now include:
   `animate_character`, `video_enhance`, `qwen_image_t2i`, `qwen_image_2512`, `qwen_image_edit`, and `z_image_turbo`.

2. Fixing real issues as they appear.
   Recent concrete fixes:
   - VibeComfy CLI compatibility: worker no longer blindly passes `--ensure-packs/--ensure-models` to older VibeComfy installs.
   - Worker failure reporting: detailed VibeComfy errors now survive into task/report output instead of being collapsed to `generation failed`.
   - RunPod harness retry: update mode now reconnects/retries if SSH drops during VibeComfy clone/install.
   - Live harness default VibeComfy branch now points at `megaplan/production-parity-templates`, not the stale sprint branch.

3. Diagnosing why the latest failure happened.
   `image_upscale` failed because the harness had been cloning an old VibeComfy branch that didn’t contain the parity template/CLI changes. I fixed that default and am retrying `image_upscale` now against the parity branch.

What’s been taking time:
- RunPod/pod lifecycle friction: pods losing SSH, stale pods becoming unmanageable, setup taking several minutes.
- Branch drift between worker code and VibeComfy templates.
- Weak error surfacing from VibeComfy/template failures.
- Repeated remote setup/install cost.

Tools/abstractions still missing or worth improving:
- A “VibeComfy environment contract check” that verifies exact VibeComfy branch/SHA, CLI features, template availability, custom node manifest, and model assets before any task is queued.
- Better VibeComfy run diagnostics: when a workflow says `run failed`, we need embedded logs/artifact metadata automatically captured.
- A reusable warm-pod mode that skips recloning/reinstalling VibeComfy when the correct SHA is already present.
- A workflow/template validator that does a real dry-run graph/materialized input check, not just structural validation.

Current live run in progress: retrying `image_upscale` on pod `spdgrt7835ecs0` after the branch-default fix.

> AGENT

No, not in the absolute sense.

What is validated now: every `vibecomfy_supported` case in the live-test matrix has at least one successful live report with an output artifact. That is 22 VibeComfy-supported cases, including:

`z_image_turbo`, `z_image_turbo_i2i`, `qwen_image`, `qwen_image_2512`, `qwen_image_edit`, `qwen_image_style`, `image_inpaint`, `annotated_image_edit`, `flux_klein_edit`, `image_upscale`, `video_enhance`, `wan_2_2_t2i`, `wan_2_2_i2v`, `animate_character`, `join_clips_segment_wan22_vace`, and the Wan VACE travel variants for raw/flow/canny/depth.

The matrix is defined in [matrix.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-worker/scripts/live_test/matrix.py:666), and the routing/template support is in [template_routing.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-worker/source/task_handlers/tasks/template_routing.py:77).

But the stronger claim, “every workflow we use in-app is validated with the same settings and same variation behavior as Wan2GP,” is not fully true yet.

Known gaps:
- Some app routes are still `wgp_only`: travel orchestrators, stitch/final stitch, join/edit orchestrators.
- Some VibeComfy-supported routes deliberately fail closed for feature params that Wan2GP can handle, including dynamic user LoRAs on some Qwen paths, too many Wan I2V LoRA slots, and non-pinned Flux Klein variants. That behavior is explicitly tested in [test_template_routing.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-worker/tests/test_template_routing.py:145).
- The live matrix validates representative route keys, not every possible app permutation of LoRA/controlnet/control-video/profile/resolution/frame-count/seed.
- The VibeComfy path uses generated Python scratchpads over Comfy templates, while Wan2GP uses its own orchestration/model handlers. We are adapting to the same contract, but not yet proving parameter-by-parameter parity everywhere.

So the status is: **all currently marked VibeComfy-supported matrix workflows are live-green, but full app parity is not proven yet.**

Next thing I’d do is a route parity audit: for each app task type, compare Wan2GP params vs VibeComfy scratchpad/template inputs for model, LoRA, control method, resolution, frames, FPS, seed, prompt/negative prompt, output contract, and fallback behavior. Then turn any mismatch into either a fix or an explicit `fail_closed` rule.
