> AGENT

The first pass exposed another root cause: schema validation was checking the pre-compile `VibeWorkflow` internals, where converted widgets may still be represented as `widget_0`, while Comfy actually receives the compiled API dict. That is the wrong abstraction level for this check. I’m moving the schema input validation to the compiled API graph, which is exactly what gets queued; that should catch runtime payload mistakes without false positives from internal representation.

Yes, for this failure class. I added `SourceSchemaProvider` and wired `vibecomfy nodes spec <ClassType>` to fall back to installed custom-node `INPUT_TYPES`, so a future agent can inspect a replacement node even when `node_index.json` is empty. The remaining improvement I still want after this run is a dedicated “compare this compiled workflow node against its spec” CLI view, but the core validation/fetch pieces are now in place.

{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/vibecomfy/vibecomfy/fetch.py\n@@\n def local_path(entry: Mapping[str, Any], *, root: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n     base = root if root is not None else models_root()\n+    target_path = entry.get(\"target_path\")\n+    if isinstance(target_path, str) and target_path:\n+        target = Path(target_path)\n+        if target.is_absolute():\n+            return target\n+        return base.parent / target\n     return base / str(entry[\"subdir\"]) / str(entry[\"name\"])\n*** End Patch\n"
}

Declare those as `model_assets` with `target_path` so `vibecomfy run` stages them before execution:\n@@\n {\"name\": \"yolox_l.onnx\", \"url\": \"...\", \"subdir\": \"controlnet_aux\", \"target_path\": \"custom_nodes/comfyui_controlnet_aux/ckpts/yzd-v/DWPose/yolox_l.onnx\"}\n ```\n \n+Loader-specific model folders matter. For example, LTX audio VAE files used by `LTXVAudioVAELoader` must be staged under `checkpoints`, not `vae`; `validate` rejects the known-bad `VAELoaderKJ` plus LTX audio VAE pairing before runtime.\n+\n For reusable workflows, the checked-in surface is Python, not raw JSON. Keep upstream/source workflows in `workflow_corpus/`, convert or author the reusable version in `ready_templates/<kind>/<id>.py`, record it in `workflow_corpus/manifests/coverage.json`, and refresh the static discovery index:\n*** End Patch\n"
}

{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/vibecomfy/docs/adding_templates_models.md\n@@\n `nodes spec` uses the generated node index when present and falls back to installed custom-node source that exposes `INPUT_TYPES`. `validate` checks the compiled API graph, not just the pre-compile Python IR, so missing required inputs and unexpected inputs are reported against the payload Comfy will actually receive when schema data is available.\n+\n+Validation also carries small runtime-compatibility gates for issues schema alone cannot express. One example is LTX audio VAE loading: use `LTXVAudioVAELoader` with the file staged under `checkpoints`; the known-bad `VAELoaderKJ` plus `LTX*_audio_vae*.safetensors` pairing is rejected before RunPod because KJNodes can misclassify that file shape as a normal VAE.\n \n Use `--head-check-models` only when you intentionally want model URL HEAD checks. Normal `port check`, `doctor`, `validate`, `fetch`, and `run` paths stay offline by default.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/vibecomfy/AGENTS.md\n@@\n Embedded runs reconcile model assets by default. If the final workflow contains a model-picker value such as `ckpt_name`, `vae_name`, `unet_name`, or `lora_name`, the runner resolves it against authored `model_assets` and `vibecomfy/registry/models.yaml` before queueing. Missing registry/authored coverage is a pre-run failure, not a Comfy queue failure. Use `--no-ensure-models` only when deliberately avoiding downloads.\n+\n+Loader folders are part of the runtime contract. If an LTX audio VAE is loaded through `LTXVAudioVAELoader`, stage it as a `checkpoints` asset. Do not load `LTX*_audio_vae*.safetensors` with `VAELoaderKJ`; `validate` rejects that pairing because current KJNodes can misclassify the file and crash at runtime.\n \n ```python\n from vibecomfy.runtime import run_embedded_sync\n result = run_embedded_sync(wf)            # blocking\n*** End Patch\n"
}

That was tested with 152 local tests and pushed.\n+\n+Goal:\n+Build and validate a robust, reusable prebuilt environment path for Reigh VibeComfy validation. It should make the rest of the parity work easier and safer, not add a rigid second source of truth.\n+\n+The target design should:\n+1. Provide a standard prebuilt environment for 4090-class RunPod validation.\n+   - Prefer RTX 4090 as the normal target because that is the user's realistic production/developer bar.\n+   - Keep the design able to run on larger GPUs when explicitly requested.\n+   - Make the environment portable when advanced kernels are unavailable, while still allowing a SageAttention-capable profile if it can be installed and validated cleanly.\n+2. Make environment dependencies explicit but not burdensome.\n+   - Capture system packages, Python version, CUDA/Torch profile, ComfyUI/VibeComfy commits, custom node lockfile state, extra model paths, optional acceleration profile, and model asset expectations in one generated or easily maintained manifest.\n+   - Avoid forcing developers to update a fragile hand-written manifest every time a workflow changes. Prefer deriving information from templates, contracts, lockfiles, and validation output.\n+4. contract evidence.\n+\n+Expected implementation shape:\n+- Improve or add CLIs/scripts around prebuilt env build/check/update/reconcile/status/cleanup.\n+- Add tests for the new behavior.\n+- Where possible, use existing abstractions in VibeComfy: template registry, model asset extraction, node lock restore, node schema inspection, workflow validation/doctor/converter tools.\n+- If missing abstractions are found, add the smallest useful abstraction that removes repeated manual friction.\n+- Keep changes scoped and avoid unrelated refactors.\n+\n+Validation requirements:\n+- Local unit tests for any changed Python modules.\n+- At least one remote RunPod prebuilt environment health check.\n+- At least one VibeComfy workflow smoke run using the prebuilt environment.\n+- Evidence > DEVELOPER

Are we tackling these problems at the right level?

> AGENT

Yes, mostly. The right level is now clearer than it was earlier:

- Workflow correctness belongs in VibeComfy: pure-Python template source, schema validation, required node inputs, source classification, model asset declarations, and expected asset paths. We fixed a bad abstraction there by making orchestrator-only targets info-only instead of fake missing-template errors.
- App parity belongs in `reigh-worker`: the matrix emits the exact app routes/cases/templates and variation dimensions, then runs them through the same queue/worker path. We added target/template counts and deterministic prebuilt selection so the app-side contract is explicit.
- Environment readiness belongs in `runpod-lifecycle`: build/check/reconcile/status/cleanup for the prebuilt RunPod volume. That is why missing assets are being resolved by `prebuilt reconcile`, not by hand-copying random files or hiding failures in workflows.

The latest friction also confirms a tooling gap at the correct layer: reconcile should not be a silent sequential SSH loop. I fixed progress, retry, and resume behavior already. If this keeps being slow after this run, the next right-level improvement is bounded parallel asset fetching inside `runpod-lifecycle`, because asset installation is environment provisioning, not workflow logic.

What I would not do is patch each workflow ad hoc to tolerate missing models or bypass validations. That would get us to a green run by weakening parity. The current direction is better: make the contracts precise, reconcile the environment against those contracts, then run the app matrix end to end.

> DEVELOPER

Are we building systematic solutions to systematic problems

> AGENT

Yes. The systematic problems we hit were: ambiguous environment selection, missing assets, false-positive workflow validation, opaque long remote operations, and report artifacts not matching the app’s actual output paths. The fixes are systematic:

- Deterministic prebuilt volume selection with `--prebuilt-data-center` instead of “first match wins”.
- VibeComfy enrichment emits model `expected_path`, URL, schema/source status, and target/template counts.
- `runpod-lifecycle prebuilt reconcile` consumes that contract and installs assets into declared paths, with resume/retry/progress.
- Live-test reports accept both linked generation rows and direct task output artifacts, matching actual Reigh task behavior.
- Orchestrator targets are classified as non-template info, so validation only blocks on actual workflow/env failures.

This is not just patching the current run. It gives future workflow onboarding a concrete loop: emit app targets, enrich in VibeComfy, reconcile env assets, health-check the prebuilt volume, run the matrix, then report exact failing case/template/asset/node. That is the right reusable shape.

  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-worker/scripts/live_test/matrix.py\n@@\n @dataclass(frozen=True)\n class MatrixCase:\n@@\n     route_runtime: RouteRuntimeOptions = field(default_factory=RouteRuntimeOptions)\n \n \n+VIBECOMFY_DEFAULT_CASE_ORDER = {\n+    \"z_image_turbo\": 0,\n+    \"z_image_turbo_i2i\": 1,\n+    \"qwen_image_2512\": 2,\n+    \"qwen_image_t2i\": 3,\n+    \"qwen_image_edit\": 4,\n+    \"qwen_image_style\": 5,\n+    \"image_inpaint\": 6,\n+    \"annotated_image_edit\": 7,\n+}\n+\n+\n+def select_cases_for_backend_default(cases: list[MatrixCase], *, backend: str, explicit_selection: bool) -> list[MatrixCase]:\n+    \"\"\"Apply the live harness default selection policy consistently.\n+\n+    A default VibeComfy run should exercise routes that the contract says\n+    VibeComfy owns. WGP-only orchestration rows stay available through explicit\n+    selection, but the harness must not silently queue them under an isolated\n+    VibeComfy selector namespace.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    if backend != \"vibecomfy\" or explicit_selection:\n+        return cases\n+\n+    filtered = [case for case in cases if case.support_state == \"vibecomfy_supported\"]\n+    return sorted(\n+        filtered,\n+        key=lambda case: VIBECOMFY_DEFAULT_CASE_ORDER.get(case.name, len(VIBECOMFY_DEFAULT_CASE_ORDER)),\n+    )\n+\n+\n def _deep_merge(base: dict[str, Any], overrides: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:\n*** End Patch\n"

> DEVELOPER

how would you make sure with absolute certainty that we have feature and setting parity with
  WAn2GP? What would the validation process look like?

> AGENT

Absolute certainty means we stop treating “workflow runs” as enough. We need a parity harness that proves, for every app capability, that VibeComfy receives the same semantic inputs, applies the same defaults/adaptations, and produces acceptable outputs under the same scenario matrix as Wan2GP.

**Validation Process**

1. **Capability Inventory**
   Build a canonical list of every app-visible generation path:
   `wan_2_2_t2i`, `wan_2_2_i2v`, travel segments, VACE control modes, LoRAs, prompt expansion, animate character, upscale, enhance, edit, etc.

   Each entry needs:
   - task type / route key
   - Wan2GP handler/source reference
   - VibeComfy template/scratchpad reference
   - supported params
   - dynamic branches: LoRA, controlnet/guidance mode, frame count, resolution, seed, start/end image, raw video, etc.

2. **Setting Contract**
   For each capability, define a machine-readable contract of the settings that must match semantically:
   - model/checkpoint
   - VAE/text encoder/CLIP/LoRA assets
   - resolution snapping
   - fps/frame count
   - sampler/scheduler/steps/cfg/shift/seed
   - guidance/control mode
   - prompt/negative prompt handling
   - input image/video handling
   - output artifact contract

   This should not duplicate every node field manually. It should capture the meaningful knobs and let validators inspect the actual generated Comfy graph/scratchpad.

3. **Static Parity Check**
   Before running anything, generate the Wan2GP effective config and the VibeComfy effective graph for the same fixture, then diff them semantically.

   This should catch:
   - missing required node inputs
   - wrong model asset
   - wrong LoRA strength
   - wrong frame count
   - JSON workflows sneaking in where pure Python is required
   - defaults that differ silently
   - unsupported branches marked as supported

4. **Node Schema Validation**
   Validate each generated VibeComfy graph against live Comfy `object_info`, not just local structural checks.

   This is what should have caught the missing node inputs earlier. The validator should fail before RunPod execution if a node requires an input we do not provide.

5. **Asset/Dependency Validation**
   Resolve every declared model/custom-node dependency before execution:
   - exact asset path
   - URL/source
   - checksum or size where available
   - expected Comfy model directory
   - custom node package/version
   - optional acceleration dependencies like `sageattention`

   Missing assets should be a preflight failure, not a runtime surprise.

6. **Golden Fixture Matrix**
   For each capability, run a minimal but representative matrix:
   - baseline/default
   - with LoRA if supported
   - with control/guidance if supported
   - with app-default resolution/frame count
   - edge case for short video / first-last images where relevant

   We do not need every combinatorial explosion, but every branch in routing/settings logic needs at least one fixture.

7. **Dual Effective-Config Comparison**
   For every fixture:
   - run Wan2GP in dry/effective-config mode
   - run VibeComfy in dry/effective-graph mode
   - compare the contract fields
   - record pass/fail in the parity ledger

   This is the core “same settings” proof.

8. **RunPod End-to-End Validation**
   Then run the VibeComfy fixture on RunPod:
   - assert task finishes
   - assert artifact exists in standard path
   - assert artifact uploads
   - assert DB task status/result is correct
   - assert logs contain no fallback/warning that changes semantics
   - inspect runtime, GPU usage, and failure mode if slow

9. **Output Quality Smoke Check**
   Use visual/video understanding where possible:
   - image exists and is not blank/corrupt
   - video has expected duration/fps/frame count
   - motion exists
   - reference/control influence is visible for relevant workflows
   - no obvious black frames or decode failures

10. **Parity Ledger**
   Keep a single tracked document or generated report with:
   - capability
   - Wan2GP source
   - VibeComfy source
   - fixture variants tested
   - static contract status
   - schema validation status
   - asset validation status
   - RunPod result
   - artifact links/paths
   - known gaps

**What “Done” Means**

A workflow is not “done” because it runs once. It is done when:

- the Wan2GP behavior has been traced to source code,
- the VibeComfy graph is pure Python,
- static contract comparison passes,
- live Comfy schema validation passes,
- required assets/custom nodes are declared and present,
- every meaningful app variation has at least one fixture,
- RunPod execution succeeds,
- output artifacts are verified,
- the parity ledger records the evidence.

For the current `animate_character` case, we are not at that bar yet. The fact that it is CPU-bound for minutes while GPU is idle is exactly the kind of issue this process should surface as a parity/performance failure, not something hidden by a longer timeout.

Without this\n+    worker-side cap, WanAnimate preprocessing can run DWPose/SAM2 over hundreds\n+    of source frames while the sampler later emits only ``frames`` frames.\n+    \"\"\"\n+\n+    if frames <= 0:\n+        return motion_name\n+    input_dir = run_workspace / \"input\"\n+    source = input_dir / motion_name\n+    source_frames = get_video_frame_count_ffprobe(str(source))\n+    if source_frames is None or source_frames <= frames:\n+        return motion_name\n+\n+    target = input_dir / f\"{Path(motion_name).stem}_first_{frames}f.mp4\"\n+    extract_frame_range_to_video(\n+        source,\n+        target,\n+        start_frame=0,\n+        end_frame=frames - 1,\n+        fps=float(fps),\n+    )\n+    headless_logger.debug(\n+        f\"[Task {task_id}] Capped animate_character motion video \"\n+        f\"from {source_frames} frames to {frames} frames for VibeComfy preprocessing\"\n+    )\n+    return target.name\n*** End Patch\n"

> DEVELOPER

And was that fixed there? Was that a hot cover or is it a well engineered solution at the right level? Can you just think that through, please?

> AGENT

Yes, this is a real fix at the right immediate level, not just a timeout cover. The bug was that our adapter let an uncapped source video enter a Comfy template whose `LoadVideo` node has no frame cap, while the rest of the graph was configured for 49 generated frames; capping the motion input before the graph means the expensive preprocessing sees the same temporal scope as generation.

The broader engineering lesson is also clear: this should become a general invariant for any workflow where a source video feeds preprocessors but generation only consumes `N` frames. The patch fixes `animate_character` specifically because that is the proven failing route; after this run, I’ll look for the same pattern across other VibeComfy scratchpads/templates and promote it into a shared helper where it applies.

> AGENT

The animate failure is now exposing a flaw in our reusable FFmpeg helper: it selects 49 source frames, then drops frames when changing 30fps source timing to 16fps output timing. That means the fix belongs below animate too: the canonical frame-range helper must preserve the selected frame count while assigning the requested output fps.

> TOOL

Wan2GP direct imports such as `shared.*` and package imports such\n+     as `Wan2GP.postprocessing.*` are both part of the worker contract.\n    - Record source URL or package source, target directory, and validated\n      environment notes such as CUDA/Torch/SageAttention availability.\n    - Prebuilt RunPod environments should be reconciled before live runs.\n@@\n 9. **Artifact inspection**\n    - Validate media metadata with `ffprobe`/image inspection: dimensions, frame\n      count, fps, duration, container, and non-empty output.\n+   - If a workflow consumes source video but generates only a bounded number of\n+     frames, validate that preprocessing is also bounded to the same effective\n+     frame count unless the source workflow intentionally needs the full clip.\n    - For visual parity, compare WGP/VibeComfy outputs with the dual-run media\n      thresholds where feasible and keep human review notes for subjective\n      differences.\n@@\n ## Current Animate Character Lesson\n \n `animate_character` exposed a process gap: increasing the live-test timeout made\n the harness wait longer, but it did not prove parity. The right signal was that\n the current VibeComfy run was CPU-hot while GPU utilization was effectively\n idle. That must be treated as a parity/performance failure until the workflow\n matches the intended Wan2GP behavior and GPU execution profile.\n+\n+The immediate fix is at the adapter/media-contract level, not as a timeout\n+cover: the app requested 49 generated frames, while the fixture motion clip had\n+774 frames. Native Comfy `LoadVideo` does not expose a frame-load cap, so the\n+worker must materialize a capped motion input before the template runs. The\n+shared `extract_frame_range_to_video` helper must also preserve selected frame\n+count when assigning a new output fps; otherwise a 30fps source capped to 49\n+frames at 16fps can silently become 28 frames.\n+\n+This is now an invariant for onboarding video-source workflows: source media\n+normalization, template frame-load caps, and generated frame count must be\n+checked together before a RunPod validation can count as parity evidence.\n+\n+## Baseline Availability\n+\n+Not every app capability has a direct Wan2GP runtime baseline that is still\n+accessible or practical to run. Record the baseline class explicitly:\n+\n+- `direct_wan2gp`: run Wan2GP and VibeComfy on the same fixture and compare\n+  settings, artifacts, and wall-clock.\n+- `wan2gp_derived`: Wan2GP source code is the behavioral reference, but a live\n+  Wan2GP run is unavailable; require effective-setting trace, VibeComfy RunPod\n+  success, artifact inspection, and a note explaining why direct timing is not\n+  available.\n+- `vibecomfy_native`: no original Wan2GP execution path exists; require app\n+  contract evidence, live schema validation, RunPod success, artifact\n+  inspection, and documented rationale.\n*** End Patch\n"

{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/vibecomfy/README.md\n@@\n python -m vibecomfy.cli validate ready_templates/<kind>/<id>.py\n python -m vibecomfy.cli port check ready_templates/<kind>/<id>.py --strict-ready-template --json\n+python -m vibecomfy.cli doctor ready_templates/<kind>/<id>.py --json\n ```\n \n The manifest/index tests catch missing ready-template rows, stale `template_index.json`, and manifest entries that point at Python templates that do not exist.\n+\n+`doctor` is the local readiness pass for a built workflow. It reports missing\n+model assets, node-pack drift, suggested patches, and runtime warnings that\n+schema validation cannot infer. For video workflows, it also flags generated\n+frame-count bindings that are paired with uncapped video loaders; either bind\n+`frame_load_cap` to the same effective frame count or have the caller\n+materialize a capped source clip before runtime.\n \n The same lifecycle applies when fixing, forking, or authoring workflows from scratch: identify the intended task and output artifact, choose recipe/patch vs new ready template, run the programmatic gates, then use agent judgment for source quality, model provenance, custom-node legitimacy, smoke adaptations, and app/Wan2GP parity before recording live evidence.\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/vibecomfy/.claude/skills/vibecomfy/SKILL.md\n@@\n - Before manually editing an imported workflow, converting raw JSON into a template, or launching RunPod validation, run `python -m vibecomfy.cli port check <workflow> --json` and use the report to resolve helper nodes, custom-node packs, schema issues, widget aliases, and model assets.\n+- Before claiming a ready template is runnable, run `python -m vibecomfy.cli doctor <workflow> --json`. Treat video frame-cap warnings as real runtime risks: if a workflow exposes `num_frames`/`video_length`/frame-count controls while loading a source video, either bind the loader's `frame_load_cap` to the effective generated frame count or have the caller materialize a capped clip before execution.\n - `vibecomfy run` reconciles model assets by default for embedded runs: it inspects the final built workflow, resolves model-picker values through `vibecomfy/registry/models.yaml`, downloads/stages what it can, and fails before queueing when a referenced asset is unresolved. Use `--no-ensure-models` only for compile-only/local work where downloads are intentionally disabled.\n@@\n python -m vibecomfy.cli validate path/to/scratchpad.py\n python -m vibecomfy.cli doctor   path/to/scratchpad.py   # requirements + readiness + suggested patches\n python -m vibecomfy.cli runtime doctor                   # runtime deps\n ```\n+\n+For source-video workflows, `doctor` warns when generated frame-count controls\n+exist but the loader can still consume the full source clip. That warning is a\n+pre-run performance/parity gate, not a cosmetic lint: resolve it by using a\n+loader with `frame_load_cap`, wiring the cap to the same effective count, or\n+normalizing the source video in the caller before Comfy preprocessors run.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

> DEVELOPER

So what would you need to do to get to 100% validated parity across all those different variables and across the various functions?

> AGENT

To get to 100% validated parity, we need a disciplined parity matrix, not more ad hoc runs.

**1. Freeze The Contract**
Define every app capability and variant we claim to support:

- task type: image, video, travel segment, join segment, enhance, animate, etc.
- model family: Wan2.2 I2V, Wan2.2 VACE, LTX, Flux/Klein, upscale
- continuity: none, first/last, video source, join bridge
- guidance/control: none, raw VACE, flow, canny, depth, LTX control video
- dynamic modifiers: LoRAs, prompt/negative prompt, seed, steps, CFG, shift, fps, frame count, resolution
- output contract: file type, dimensions, frame count, fps, artifact path

This contract already mostly exists, but 9 VibeComfy routes are still static-only.

**2. Validate Settings Parity**
For each supported route, compare Wan2GP source behavior against VibeComfy:

- selected model/checkpoints/VAEs/text encoders
- sampler, scheduler, steps, CFG, shift, seeds
- LoRA injection behavior and strengths
- control/video preprocessing behavior
- frame count, fps, dimensions, resize/crop policy
- memory/offload/profile settings
- output postprocessing

This should produce a “parity reviewed” entry per route, not just “it ran.”

**3. Run End-To-End Evidence**
Run all remaining live cases on owned RunPod machines only:

- rerun the 9 missing VibeComfy cases
- promote only reports with final status `Complete`
- discard reports where pod vanished, task was manually killed, or worker errored externally
- fetch artifacts and verify metadata: duration, fps, frame count, resolution, non-empty video/image

**4. Run Wan2GP Comparison**
For speed/cost parity, run matched Wan2GP and VibeComfy cases on the same GPU class:

- preferably 4090, warm-cache/prebuilt environment
- same input assets
- same seed/settings where meaningful
- record setup time separately from inference time
- compare generation wall-clock, GPU class, hourly rate, output metadata

Cold model downloads cannot be included in “generation parity”; they’re environment provisioning cost.

**5. Fix Remaining Gaps**
For every failed/mismatched route:

- determine if it is a code bug, template bug, model dependency issue, pod infra issue, or contract mismatch
- fix at the shared abstraction level
- add a regression test or contract warning so it cannot silently recur
- rerun only the failed cases until clean

**6. Final Gate**
We can call 100% only when:

- `scripts.capability_contracts.report validate` has zero warnings/errors for VibeComfy-supported routes
- all VibeComfy-supported live matrix cases have latest passing RunPod reports
- artifacts are fetched and metadata-validated
- parity tracker says every app capability is runtime-green or explicitly WGP-only/unsupported
- timing/cost comparison is recorded for representative Wan2GP-vs-VibeComfy routes

The immediate next move is to get stable owned RunPod capacity, ideally a 4090 or prebuilt 4090-like environment, then rerun the 9 remaining cases from the patched branches.

> AGENT

I found a more fundamental issue: the production orchestrator’s zombie/externally-terminated check is marking our live-test worker row as error when RunPod listing does not include the live-test pod. The harness then sees that DB error, exits, and only then terminates its own pod. So the failed report is likely a control-plane interference/false positive, not a VibeComfy workflow failure. I’m going to patch that at the orchestrator boundary so live-test-owned workers are not failed by the production zombie check while they are being validated.

> DEVELOPER

Are we approaching this in a smart and well-structured way? are you confident that this approach wll get us to 100% adherence?

> AGENT

Yes, with one qualification: the structure is right now because we’re separating three different things that were previously tangled together: contract/static parity, live execution evidence, and runtime/cost parity. That is the only way to get to defensible 100% adherence instead of “it ran once, probably fine.”

What I’m doing now is deliberately evidence-driven:

- Branch/base is pinned explicitly for every run: worker parity branch, VibeComfy parity-template branch, and deployed orchestrator branch with the live-test exclusion fix.
- The contract tells us which cases still need live evidence; we’re driving the remaining nine from that list rather than ad hoc testing.
- The RunPod run is using the app path, selector routing, generated Python scratchpads, model resolution, worker claiming, artifact/output path, and real VibeComfy execution.
- I’m not marking a workflow green until the actual report says it passed, and I’m watching wall-clock/GPU behavior because feature parity without performance parity is not enough here.

The qualification: I’m not yet confident we’re at 100%, because this run is exposing a likely runtime performance/config issue. It is making progress and cases are completing, but Wan/VACE is much slower than the 2-3 minute target. So the approach will get us to 100% adherence, but only if we treat slow-but-passing as a real parity gap to investigate, not as a success.

After this run finishes, the next structured steps are:
1. Update the parity contract from the report, only for cases that actually passed.
2. Record wall-clock/runtime evidence in the runbook.
3. Compare the same settings against Wan2GP where accessible.
4. Fix either workflow settings, attention/runtime config, model/profile selection, or prebuilt environment if that’s the cause of the slowdown.
5. Rerun until the contract is green and timing is explainable.

I’m continuing the run now; I won’t claim completion until the evidence supports it.

> DEVELOPER

And on it being slower is that because we're not using like the, where we have a misconfigured environment or because we're, um, we're, um. Or because we're not doing the right distillation approach with light high 2x for some other reason?

> AGENT

Most likely it is not “distillation approach” for the cases currently running. The slow cases so far are Wan 2.2 VACE paths, and the generated scratchpad is using `Wan2_2-T2V-A14B-HIGH_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled_KJ.safetensors` plus `Wan2_1-VACE_module_14B_fp8_e4m3fn.safetensors`, 81 frames at 832x480, 6 steps. That sounds like the heavy Wan/VACE path, not LTX2/LTX distilled inference.

The plausible causes, in order, are:

- Runtime/env config: we’re using the portable attention profile with `attention_mode='sdpa'`, not necessarily the fastest 4090 path. If Wan2GP used a faster attention/kernel stack, compiled ops, sageattention, TeaCache, or offload settings, VibeComfy can pass but be much slower.
- Workflow setting parity gap: we may be using Wan2.2 HIGH/VACE settings where Wan2GP used a lighter low/high split, reduced frames, cache, or different step schedule. This is exactly why we need the Wan2GP setting comparison before calling parity.
- First-run overhead inside each task: VibeComfy is invoked as a fresh process per task with `--ensure-packs --ensure-models`; if startup/model validation/cache load happens every task, that can add minutes even when models are present.
- Hardware/profile mismatch: a 4090 can run it, but if memory pressure forces CPU/offload or serialized attention, it will be dramatically slower.

So I would not assume “wrong distillation” yet. I’d test it by extracting the exact generated scratchpad settings and comparing them to Wan2GP’s route/settings for the same capability, then inspect VibeComfy runtime logs for attention/offload/cache decisions. The current run is giving us the concrete cases and timings to do that instead of guessing.

The LTX2 case is also spending several minutes in CPU-side VibeComfy execution with almost no GPU allocation yet. That points more strongly to per-task VibeComfy startup/model-pack/validation overhead or environment configuration, not just Wan/VACE model heaviness.

I found another infrastructure root cause: the lifecycle storage expansion helper only expands volumes below 100 GB. For prebuilt builds, that is the wrong abstraction; the builder asks for a target volume size, and existing volumes smaller than that target should be expanded before provisioning. I’m fixing that so prebuilt builds can make the storage contract explicit instead of failing mid-bundle with disk quota exceeded.

> AGENT

This is now clearly a pre-inference model/session startup bottleneck, not diffusion inference. The spawned embedded Comfy process has ~31 GB RSS and ~370 CPU threads, while GPU is effectively idle; it is cold-loading / initializing the LTX graph and model stack in a one-shot subprocess. That is a deeper architectural parity gap: Wan2GP runs as a persistent worker and can keep heavyweight model state warm, while the current VibeComfy adapter launches a fresh CLI process per task.

> DEVELOPER

wait, why is video/ltx2_3_runexx_first_last_raw_video_guide.py not proper python?

> AGENT

It is proper Python in the VibeComfy sense: the file is a `build() -> VibeWorkflow` template that constructs nodes and edges programmatically, not an embedded `API_WORKFLOW = {...}` JSON blob. The pure-Python guard is also in the test suite (`test_ready_templates_are_pure_python_builders`) and it passed after this change.

The part that may look suspicious is that it was converted from a Comfy graph and still has literal node ids like `"2152"` and `"6101"`. That’s acceptable for now because the worker patches those ids as a stable runtime contract; it is still editable Python, but not yet “beautiful semantic builder” Python. The current parity priority is correctness and live validation; after this LTX run completes, the cleanup I’d do is introduce named constants or small helper builders so those ids are documented and less brittle.

> DEVELOPER

So is everything now running at the same speed with the exact same settings across all the different things that's accessible inside of Ray?

> AGENT

No. What we have now is **contract-clean functional parity evidence** for the current VibeComfy-supported app routes: they run end-to-end on RunPod, upload artifacts, and the parity contract has no live-evidence gaps.

What we do **not** yet have is a fully proven claim that every route runs with:
- the exact same effective settings as Wan2GP,
- the same sampler/model/offload/precision behavior,
- the same wall-clock or inference speed,
- the same GPU cost profile,
- and paired Wan2GP vs VibeComfy timing evidence for every accessible Reigh path.

The latest evidence actually shows this still needs work:
- LTX control-video passed, but took about `1099s` generation window on A100.
- Wan I2V passed, about `686s` generation window on A100.
- Some earlier LTX evidence on RTX 4090 was around `670s`.
- These are valid functional runs, but they are not yet “same speed/cost as Wan2GP” proof.

So the precise status is:

**Yes:** VibeComfy routes currently tracked by the contract are running end-to-end and contract validation is clean.

**No:** We have not yet completed exhaustive Wan2GP setting-by-setting and timing-by-timing parity for every accessible Reigh capability.

The next step for that bar is paired validation: run Wan2GP and VibeComfy for the same selected cases, same input assets, same resolution/frames/LoRAs/control modes, capture effective settings and generation timing, then compare route by route.

> DEVELOPER

Does this point to some kind of deeper issue? Are the two approaches smoothly interchangable here?

> AGENT

Yes. This exposed a real deeper issue: we had conflated three identities that need to stay separate.

`task_type` is the app capability, like `wan_2_2_i2v`. `model` is the backend-loadable model identity, which for WGP must be something Wan2GP can load, like `wan_2_2_i2v_lightning_baseline_2_2_2`. `template_id` is the VibeComfy implementation choice, like `video/wanvideo_wrapper_22_14b_i2v_kijai`.

Those are not smoothly interchangeable if they share one field. The well-engineered version is exactly what we’re moving toward: app code asks for a capability, routing selects a backend, then each backend receives its own native execution identity. WGP should never see a Comfy template id as `model`; VibeComfy should never require a Wan2GP default json as its template. The contract should verify those boundaries before live runs.

I’ve fixed the immediate catalog leak and added a regression test, but I’m still validating the live retry now to prove the fix on RunPod.

> AGENT

I found the real systematic miss: the scratchpad was setting visible widget fields, but linked Comfy constants were still driving the graph. The rendered metadata shows VibeComfy actually ran 6 steps, split at 3, and phase-1 CFG schedule `2.0`, despite the scratchpad text saying 4/2/3.0. That is exactly why source-string validation was insufficient; I’m fixing the scratchpad to update the actual constant/schedule inputs and adding tests that inspect the effective rendered prompt, not just the generated Python text.

The missing metadata is not a VibeComfy runtime failure; VibeComfy writes `out/runs/<run>/metadata.json` under its own cwd, while the worker’s per-task folder only kept the scratchpad and final media. > AGENT

I found the likely root cause: the earlier shutdown timeout wrapped `Comfy.__aexit__` in `asyncio.wait_for`, which runs the coroutine in a different asyncio context. Comfy’s own context manager later resets a `ContextVar` token created during `__aenter__`, so the reset fails and suppresses the successful run result before metadata is printed. The proper fix is to keep `__aexit__` in the original context and put the timeout around the slow cleanup future inside Comfy’s embedded client instead.

_materialize_wgp_asset_urls(queue: \"HeadlessTaskQueue\", task_id: str, wgp_params: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:\n+    \"\"\"Download WGP asset URL params before Wan2GP's local-file preflight runs.\"\"\"\n+    asset_dir = _wgp_asset_dir(queue, task_id)\n+    for param in WGP_IMAGE_ASSET_PARAMS:\n+        if param in wgp_params:\n+            wgp_params[param] = _materialize_asset_value(\n+ output_root = getattr(queue, \"main_output_dir\", None)\n+    base = Path(output_root) if output_root else Path(queue.wan_dir) / \"reigh_inputs\"\n+    return base / str(task_id)\n+\n+\n+def _materialize_asset_value(value: Any, downloader) -> Any:\n+    if isinstance(value, str):\n+        return downloader(value)\n+    if isinstance(value, list):\n+        return [_materialize_asset_value(item, downloader) for item in value]\n+    if isinstance(value, tuple):\n+        return tuple(_materialize_asset_value(item, downloader) for item in value)\n+    return value\n*** End Patch\n"

> DEVELOPER

is that including the model load time, etc.?

> AGENT

For the speed table I’m using `elapsed_sec`, which includes the full task wall-clock window: conversion/materialization, model switching/loading if needed, inference, output handling, upload, and DB completion. That is intentional for cross-backend parity because the current `generation_elapsed_sec` boundaries are not equivalent between Wan2GP and VibeComfy.

For diagnosis, I’m also recording phase evidence where available. Example from corrected Wan I2V: WGP elapsed was `421.965s`, WGP `generation_elapsed_sec` was `121.901s`, while VibeComfy elapsed was `466.902s` and Vibe metadata showed subprocess `454.099s`, queue/sampling/model-work `443.991s`. So the parity verdict uses elapsed; the root-cause analysis breaks down load/inference where logs allow it.

> AGENT

The biggest VACE gap is now clearly architectural, not a sampler setting: WGP keeps the model hot inside the worker across queued cases, while the VibeComfy worker path is launching a VibeComfy subprocess per task, which reloads/patches the graph each time. That explains why the WGP second VACE case is `173s` and VibeComfy’s analogous case is `707s`. I’m checking the adapter to decide whether the right fix is a persistent VibeComfy runtime inside the worker, or a narrower template/runtime optimization.

> DEVELOPER

Does this point to some kind of structural issue?

> AGENT

Yes, it points to a structural issue, not just an isolated typo. The session runtime assumed “ComfyUI installed” meant “the `comfyui` console script exists,” but our embedded/subprocess path has been running through Python modules, so the prebuilt environment could pass embedded validation while still being unable to launch the persistent server. That’s exactly the kind of environment-contract mismatch the tooling should catch.

> AGENT

The fix is to make the runtime executable contract explicit and testable: session startup must resolve to either a real `comfyui` script or a Python module fallback, and the preflight should include that check whenever session mode is enabled. I’m making the fallback robust first, then I’ll add the worker/preflight guard so this cannot reach a live run again.

This exposes the actual root: `python -m comfy.cmd.cli` is the wrong module form. That file defines `entrypoint()` but has no `if __name__ == "__main__"` call, so `python -m comfy.cmd.cli serve ...` exits or idles without starting the server. The proper module target is `python -m comfy.cmd.main`, which delegates into the CLI entrypoint. I’m fixing the resolver and preflight to validate the executable module form, not just package importability.

> DEVELOPER

do you have a way to sweep all availabilities/relevant regions  to find cthe cheapeeast possible? And what about the datacenteres where we have storage?

> AGENT

That’s exactly the missing operational tool. We have pieces in `runpod-lifecycle` for GPU lookup and network volumes, but the current live-test launcher is still too narrow: it targets one data center/volume and one GPU type. I’m checking the lifecycle package now to see whether we already expose a capacity/price sweep, and if not I’ll add/use the smallest useful version before rerunning.

> AGENT

Yes, partially, and this is the right abstraction boundary:

- We already have `runpod-lifecycle probe`, which sweeps RunPod’s GPU types without launching and returns currently launchable options ranked by price.
- We already have `runpod-lifecycle prebuilt list`, which tells us which data centers have Reigh prebuilt storage volumes.
- What we do **not** yet have is the combined planner: “given the volumes we already have, find the cheapest compatible GPU/data-center pair and launch there.”

Current facts from the tools:
- Prebuilt portable volumes exist in `CA-MTL-3` and `EUR-NO-1`.
- Global secure-cloud probe currently shows cheaper available GPUs than A100: A5000 `$0.27/hr`, L4 `$0.39/hr`, A40 `$0.44/hr`, L40S `$0.86/hr`, RTX 5090 `$0.99/hr`, A100 SXM `$1.49/hr`.
- RTX 4090 is not showing in the global secure-cloud probe right now, and it is also failing capacity in `CA-MTL-3`.

The missing tool should combine those two sources, then try only data centers where we have the relevant prebuilt volume. I’m checking whether the live-test harness can already take a candidate GPU list and alternate data center; if not, I’ll add the small planner rather than keep manually poking one region.

> AGENT

Yes. The systematic issue is that runtime accelerators and node-pack-specific dependencies were treated as an environment profile, not as workflow-declared requirements. I’ve started fixing that by making the LTX template declare `sageattention`, making the live-test harness install/verify SageAttention-ada when a selected template needs it, and keeping the route key unchanged.

The broader VibeComfy/Astrid improvement should be: every workflow exposes a small machine-readable runtime contract: model assets, custom nodes, Python packages, runtime flags, expected output artifacts, and validation evidence. Astrid then consumes that contract to preflight before running, fetch outputs consistently, and use media-understanding checks after generation. Right now those pieces exist in fragments; this work is turning them into the path the app actually uses.

> DEVELOPER

So what would the 'proper' solution ehre look liek taht would sovle this + other problems?

> AGENT

The proper solution is a workflow runtime contract that is generated from the Python workflow, not maintained as a separate spreadsheet. It should have one canonical object with these sections: `assets` (models/input fixtures/output paths), `nodes` (required packs and pinned versions), `python_packages` (SageAttention-ada, onnxruntime, etc.), `runtime_flags` (`--use-sage-attention`, memory profile, cache policy), `schema_requirements` (required inputs and accepted node widgets), and `evidence` (last RunPod GPU, wall time, generation time, VRAM peak, output artifacts, media checks).

Then every tool uses that same object:
- `vibecomfy doctor` validates required inputs, node schemas, packages, model paths, output saves, and pure-Python policy before runtime.
- `vibecomfy reconcile` installs/stages declared models, node packs, and Python packages into the target environment.
- `reigh live-test` refuses to queue work until the contract is satisfied, and records timing/VRAM/output evidence back into the contract evidence log.
- Astrid consumes the output-artifact contract, fetches generated media, and runs image/video-understanding checks against route-specific expectations.

That would have prevented this specific issue because the LTX template enabling `PathchSageAttentionKJ(auto)` would have declared `sageattention` and the preflight would either install SageAttention-ada or fail before the app task ran. It also covers missing models, wrong model folders, missing required node inputs, JSON-vs-Python violations, missing output files, and “it ran but produced the wrong kind of artifact.”

{
  "cmd": "megaplan ticket new \"First-class workflow runtime contracts for VibeComfy/Reigh/Astrid\" --tags cross-repo,workflow-contracts,vibecomfy,astrid,runpod,validation - <<'EOF'\nWe need a first-class workflow runtime contract abstraction for VibeComfy that is generated from, or attached to, each Python ready workflow and then consumed consistently by VibeComfy doctor/reconcile, the Reigh live-test harness, the worker runtime, and Astrid result validation.\n\nContext from the current Wan2GP parity push:\n- LTX Runexx first/last workflows were valid Python workflows and produced outputs, but were far slower than Wan2GP on the same 4090.\n- The root cause was not just a bad sampler value: the workflow enabled a Comfy/KJNodes runtime path where speed depends on SageAttention, while the prebuilt validation environment was still treated as a generic portable environment.\n- The contract/doctor layer could detect that uncontracted SageAttention was unsafe, but there was no generic way for the workflow to declare \"this route requires SageAttention-ada and --use-sage-attention\" and have every consumer install, validate, and run with that requirement.\n- The fix in progress is a narrow slice: add `runtime_packages` metadata to the LTX Runexx template, enable `PathchSageAttentionKJ(auto)`, make prebuilt live-test install/verify SageAttention-ada before launching, and set the Sage attention env for the worker without mutating the route key. That solves the immediate case, but it is still bespoke.\n\nThe proper abstraction should be a single machine-readable runtime contract per workflow/template, not scattered checks. It should cover at least:\n- Asset contract: model files, exact loader-facing paths/subdirs, input fixtures, output artifact names/prefixes, and expected media kinds.\n- Node contract: required custom-node packs, lockfile pins, relevant node class versions or object_info compatibility requirements.\n- Python package contract: runtime Python packages and install sources, e.g. SageAttention-ada, onnxruntime, opencv variants, audio deps, with install/verify probes.\n- Runtime flag contract: memory profile, cache policy, reserve VRAM, `--use-sage-attention`, attention profile, Comfy/HiddenSwitch flags, and route-specific environment knobs.\n- Schema/input contract: required node inputs, accepted widget names/values, missing connection detection, and family-specific override eligibility.\n- Output contract: where generated media must land, what filenames/prefixes are valid, what the app/Astrid should fetch, and how to fail when a run succeeds but no artifact appears.\n- Evidence contract: last validated GPU, RunPod pod/profile, wall clock, generation-only time, VRAM/RAM peaks, backend version/commit SHAs, output artifact paths, and media-understanding validation status.\n- Policy contract: pure-Python workflow source only for app-active routes; raw JSON may remain source/reference material but must not be the runtime path.\n\nEvery relevant tool should consume the same contract:\n- `vibecomfy doctor` should validate required inputs/connections, object_info compatibility, pure-Python policy, package requirements, model paths, output sinks, and runtime flags before execution.\n- `vibecomfy reconcile` should stage/download assets, install/restore node packs, install declared Python packages, verify imports/kernels, and report what remains manual.\n- Reigh live-test should refuse to queue app tasks until the runtime contract is satisfied; it should install/verify declared runtime packages on prebuilt consumers or fail early with actionable errors.\n- Reigh worker should select templates/routes independently from runtime installation profiles. Runtime package needs must not mutate product route keys like `profile-default`.\n- Astrid should consume the output/evidence section to fetch generated files and run image/video understanding checks against route-specific expectations.\n- The contract should remain lightweight enough that adding/forking workflows is not bureaucratic: defaults should be inferred from the Python graph where possible, and authors should only declare what cannot be inferred.\n\nAcceptance criteria for an implementation epic:\n1. Add a typed/runtime-contract model in VibeComfy and expose it from ready workflows, preferably by normalizing existing `READY_METADATA`, `READY_REQUIREMENTS`, model asset declarations, and runtime configuration fields rather than inventing a parallel spreadsheet.\n2. Migrate the LTX Runexx SageAttention requirement from bespoke metadata/harness logic into the generic contract model, while preserving the current SageAttention-ada behavior.\n3. Teach doctor/porting analysis to report missing package/runtime flag requirements as first-class contract failures with clear remediation.\n4. Teach reconcile/prebuilt build/consumer launch to install and verify declared Python packages and runtime flags before queueing work.\n5. Teach output artifact validation to use the same contract so successful process exit without expected media fails clearly.\n6. Record validation evidence back to a durable evidence artifact or contract-adjacent log after RunPod runs, including generation time and VRAM peak where available.\n7. Add tests showing this would have prevented: uncontracted SageAttention, missing required node inputs/connections, missing model folders, wrong output path/prefix, JSON runtime source for app-active workflows, and route-key pollution from diagnostic runtime params.\n8. Document the workflow authoring/onboarding checklist around this contract for new workflows, forked workflows, and workflows converted from upstream JSON.\n\nThis is cross-repo: VibeComfy should own the contract schema and doctor/reconcile behavior; Reigh worker/live-test should consume it; Astrid should consume output/evidence contracts for result validation.\nEOF",

Yes. The root issue I’ve isolated so far is not “one slow run”; it is two mismatches in the validation system: live-test defaulted VibeComfy to memory profile `3` while app/orchestrator defaults to profile `1`, and the prebuilt reattach path re-extracts the VibeComfy venv before every run, which deletes SageAttention and forces a 10-minute reinstall. I’m validating the profile hypothesis now, then I’ll patch the harness so future parity runs use the same profile as production and do not silently measure the wrong runtime mode.

Keep extraction idempotent for an unchanged bundle so those\n+    repairs are not destroyed before every run.\n+    \"\"\"\n     target_parent = target_path.rsplit(\"/\", 1)[0] or \"/\"\n+    marker_path = f\"{target_path.rstrip('/')}/.reigh_bundle_sha256\"\n     sha_script = (\n         \"set -euo pipefail\\n\"\n         f\"sha256sum {_quote(bundle_path)} | awk '{{print $1}}'\\n\"\n     )\n@@\n             \"extract_bundle_to_container_disk sha256 mismatch for \"\n             f\"{bundle_path}: expected {expected_sha256}, observed {observed!r}\"\n         )\n     extract_script = (\n         \"set -euo pipefail\\n\"\n+        f\"if [ -d {_quote(target_path)} ] && [ -f {_quote(marker_path)} ] && [ \\\"$(cat {_quote(marker_path)})\\\" = {_quote(observed)} ]; then\\n\"\n+        \"  exit 0\\n\"\n+        \"fi\\n\"\n         f\"mkdir -p {_quote(target_parent)}\\n\"\n         f\"rm -rf {_quote(target_path)}\\n\"\n         f\"mkdir -p {_quote(target_path)}\\n\"\n         f\"if command -v pv >/dev/null 2>&1; then\\n\"\n         f\"  pv {_quote(bundle_path)} | tar --use-compress-program 'zstd -d --threads=0' -xf - -C {_quote(target_path)} --strip-components=1\\n\"\n         f\"else\\n\"\n         f\"  tar --use-compress-program 'zstd -d --threads=0' -xf {_quote(bundle_path)} -C {_quote(target_path)} --strip-components=1\\n\"\n         f\"fi\\n\"\n+        f\"printf '%s\\\\n' {_quote(observed)} > {_quote(marker_path)}\\n\"\n     )\n*** End Patch\n"

> AGENT

Yes. I searched local corpus, upstream repos, and `$hivemind`.

Finding: there does not appear to be a separate “official/Kijai first-last Wan2GP-equivalent” workflow. Kijai’s LTX2.3 discussion points to RuneXX for FLF/FMLF first-last workflows, while the official Lightricks repo provides the cleaner Wan2GP-like base: `LTX-2.3_T2V_I2V_Two_Stage_Distilled.json`.

Best path:
- Use official Lightricks two-stage distilled I2V as the base execution graph.
- Add only the first/last-frame mechanism from RuneXX/Kijai discussion as a small adaptation layer.
- Do not keep trying to tune the full RuneXX graph into parity; it has extra audio, guide, tuner, GGUF/orphan loader, and chunking machinery that makes it structurally different from Wan2GP.

> AGENT

We do have conversion tools. The problem is they mostly convert JSON into **literal Python graph construction**, not into a clean semantic workflow API.

Current tools:

- `tools/convert_ready_templates.py`
  Converts legacy `API_WORKFLOW` / `NODES` templates into Python files.

- `vibecomfy.porting.emitter.emit_ready_template_python`
  Emits `wf.node(...)` calls with preserved node IDs and edges.

- `tools/format_as_python.py`
  Older/compat emitter path for formatting a workflow as Python.

- `vibecomfy.porting.workbench`
  Inspects/imports workflow JSON, analyzes assets, custom nodes, widgets, and porting issues.

- `ready_template_source_info(...)`
  Detects whether a template is pure Python, JSON reference, JSON runtime wrapper, etc.

- `test_ready_templates_are_pure_python_builders`
  Catches obvious “JSON blob embedded in Python” regressions.

Why they’re incomplete:

They answer “can this JSON be materialized as Python?” but not “is this now a pleasant, semantic, editable workflow?” The generated output is still basically:

```python
_node(wf, "LTXVImgToVideoConditionOnly", "4970", ...)
wf.replace_edge("4970.image", ...)
```

That is technically pure Python, but it is still node-ID-level graph surgery. It does not give us first-class concepts like:

```python
workflow.stage(1).condition_on(start_image, strength=1.0)
workflow.stage(2).condition_on(end_image, strength=1.0)
workflow.set_wan2gp_sigmas(...)
workflow.expose_reigh_patch_points(...)
```

So the missing layer is a **semantic workflow authoring/editing layer** on top of the converted graph.

Why I ended up doing “JSON hacking shit”:

The compiled Comfy payload is JSON-shaped because Comfy executes JSON-shaped node graphs. I used compiled API assertions in a test to verify links. That was the wrong level for the test. It made the test read like compiled JSON is the source of truth, when the source of truth should be the Python `VibeWorkflow`.

Correct approach from here:

- Use converted templates only as raw material.
- Build/maintain app-facing workflows as pure Python templates.
- Add helpers/contracts that assert graph semantics from `VibeWorkflow`, not raw compiled API blobs.
- Compile to API only as a final runtime smoke check.
- Add a validator that fails if a ready template embeds `API_WORKFLOW`, calls `workflow_from_api`, loads JSON at runtime, or relies on JSON wrappers.

So: the tools exist, but they stop one level too low. We need to add the missing semantic workflow editing/validation layer, and I should use that instead of testing or patching through raw compiled API links.

It should plug in as a thin semantic layer above `VibeWorkflow`, not replace the existing converter.

**What We Have**
`JSON/UI workflow -> convert_to_vibe_format -> VibeWorkflow -> emit_ready_template_python -> ready_template -> compile("api") -> Comfy runtime`

That pipeline is useful. The missing piece is:

`VibeWorkflow -> semantic workflow lens/contracts -> clean edits + parity validation`

**What Would Make This Easy**
Add a `vibecomfy.workflow_lens` package with small typed helpers:

```python
from vibecomfy.workflow_lens import WorkflowLens

lens = WorkflowLens(workflow)

lens.input("start_image").bind_load_image("2004")
lens.input("end_image").bind_load_image("47")

lens.conditioning.stage(1).uses_image("start_image").strength("first_frame_strength")
lens.conditioning.stage(2).uses_image("end_image").strength("last_frame_strength")

lens.sampling.stage(2).sigmas("0.909375, 0.725, 0.421875, 0.0")

Then tests become:

contract.assert_input("start_image")
contract.assert_input("end_image")

contract.assert_conditioning(stage=2, image="end_image")

No raw `api["3336"]["inputs"]["image"] == ["4990", 0]` in app-facing tests.

**How It Plugs In**
1. **Converter output**
   After `convert_ready_templates.py` emits raw Python, run:
   ```bash
   python -m vibecomfy.workflow_lens suggest video/ltx2_3_lightricks_two_stage
   ```
   It detects likely prompt/image/seed/sampler/output nodes and proposes semantic bindings.

2. **Manual template authoring**
   Templates can keep node IDs internally, but expose intent:
   ```python
   bind_ltx_first_last_contract(wf, first_image="2004", last_image="47", ...)
   ```

3. **Validation**
   Add:
   ```bash
   python -m vibecomfy.workflow_lens validate --all-ready
   ```
   It checks:
   - pure Python source
   - required patch points exist
   - no missing required edges
   - no unbound app inputs
   - expected model assets/custom nodes declared
   - runtime API compiles

   For Reigh:

Keep it boring and composable:

- `workflow_lens/graph.py`: ergonomic node/edge queries.
- `workflow_lens/contracts.py`: semantic assertions.
- `workflow_lens/ltx.py`: LTX-specific helpers like first/last, two-stage, IC-LoRA.

ANd do we not already have something similar to this...somewhere in VibeComfy?

I’ll check the actual VibeComfy modules before answering, because there are pieces that sound close: porting workbench, template source diagnostics, route contracts, schema validation, and patch helpers. The important question is whether any of them already provide the semantic “workflow lens” layer, or only adjacent plumbing.

> AGENT

Yes. There are several pieces that are close, but none is quite the thing we need.

What already exists:

- `vibecomfy.analysis.graph`
  This is probably the closest naming-wise. It gives graph analysis utilities, but it does not appear to be a full semantic contract layer for “stage 1 conditions on first image, stage 2 conditions on last image.”

- `vibecomfy.blocks.*`
  This is an authored workflow-building abstraction. It helps create workflows from reusable blocks. Useful, but it does not wrap converted/community workflows with semantic introspection and parity assertions.

- `vibecomfy.ops.image` / `vibecomfy.ops.video`
  Higher-level operation dispatch. Good for “generate video from inputs,” but not enough for inspecting/forking a particular Comfy graph and validating app parity.

- `vibecomfy.patches.*`
  Reusable graph mutation layer. This is close to the right extension point. Existing patches do things like resolution, seed, LTX low-VRAM, requirements, ControlNet. But patches are mostly mutation helpers, not semantic contracts.

- `vibecomfy.porting.workbench`
  Very important existing tool. It already checks source shape, custom nodes, model assets, required runtime inputs, widget aliases, schema validation, etc. This is the onboarding/doctor layer.

- `vibecomfy.schema.validate`
  Catches missing required inputs, unknown inputs, link shape/type issues against node schemas. This is the right low-level validator.

- `ready_template_source_info`
  Already catches JSON runtime wrappers / API dict wrappers and classifies pure Python. This directly addresses part of the “why are we allowing JSON nonsense?” issue.

So the honest answer: we have **80% of the raw machinery**, but not the top-level ergonomic abstraction.

The missing thing should probably not be a totally new subsystem. It should plug into these existing pieces as:

```text
porting.workbench
  -> source/import/schema/model/custom-node diagnostics

analysis.graph
  -> reusable graph query helpers

patches
  -> reusable mutations

NEW: contracts / lenses
  -> semantic assertions and named workflow concepts

ready_template_source_info + validate
  -> CI/preflight gates
```

The clean version would be something like:

```python
from vibecomfy.contracts import WorkflowContract
from vibecomfy.contracts.ltx import ltx_first_last_two_stage

contract = ltx_first_last_two_stage(
    start_image="start_image",
    end_image="end_image",
    stage1_condition_node="3159",
    stage2_condition_node="4970",
    stage2_sigmas="0.909375, 0.725, 0.421875, 0.0",
)

contract.validate(workflow)
```

And internally that uses `analysis.graph`, `workflow.inputs`, `workflow.edges`, and `schema.validate`.

What would have made this a breeze is a command like:

```bash
python -m vibecomfy.cli contract inspect video/ltx2_3_lightricks_two_stage
python -m vibecomfy.cli contract apply --pattern ltx-first-last-two-stage \
  video/ltx2_3_lightricks_two_stage \
  --out video/ltx2_3_lightricks_first_last_parity
python -m vibecomfy.cli contract validate video/ltx2_3_lightricks_first_last_parity
```

So: yes, we have related tooling. The mistake was not leaning hard enough on the existing workbench/schema/source-info stack, and the gap is a small “semantic contract/lens” layer tying those tools together in the language of workflows rather than node soup.

> DEVELOPER

So what would an excellent overall shape for this tooling look like? How would the agent perceive that? What are the missing pices?

> DEVELOPER

How would it all fit together? What's the right surface?

> AGENT

The right surface is not “another converter.” It is a **workflow onboarding and parity system** built around the existing VibeComfy pieces.

**Overall Shape**
```text
1. Discover
   Find official/community workflows, source URLs, node packs, models.

2. Port Check
   Run existing `port check` / schema / model / custom-node diagnostics.

3. Convert
   Materialize source workflow into pure Python ready template.

4. Lens
   Interpret the graph in workflow concepts:
   prompt, negative, seed, dimensions, inputs, stages, controls, LoRAs, output.

5. Contract
   Declare what the app route requires:
   first frame goes here, last frame goes there, stage-2 sigmas match Wan2GP,
   LoRAs are applied this way, control video routes this way.

6. Validate
   Validate source purity, semantic contract, schema, model assets, runtime API.

7. Run
   Execute local/RunPod smoke and production-size tests.

8. Compare
   Compare Wan2GP vs VibeComfy: settings, wall time, inference time, VRAM,
   output artifact presence, and qualitative media sanity.
```

**Agent-Facing Surface**
The agent should see one obvious command family:

```bash
vibecomfy workflow inspect <source-or-template>
vibecomfy workflow port-check <source-or-template>
vibecomfy workflow convert <source-json> --as video/foo
vibecomfy workflow lens <template>
vibecomfy workflow contract validate <template> --contract reigh/route.yaml
vibecomfy workflow parity run <route> --backend vibecomfy
vibecomfy workflow parity compare <route> --baseline wan2gp
```

And one obvious doc/checklist:

```text
To onboard or fork a workflow:
1. inspect
2. port-check
3. convert
4. add/apply contract
5. validate
6. run smoke
7. run app-sized test
8. compare against reference
```

**Developer Surface**
In Python, it should look like this:

```python
from vibecomfy.contracts.ltx import LTXFirstLastTwoStageContract

contract = LTXFirstLastTwoStageContract(
    start_image="start_image",
    end_image="end_image",
    prompt="prompt",
    negative="negative",
    seed=("seed", "stage2_seed"),
    dimensions=("width", "height", "frames", "fps"),
    stage1_condition="first_frame",
    stage2_condition="last_frame",
    stage2_sigmas="0.909375, 0.725, 0.421875, 0.0",
)

contract.validate(workflow)
```

Template code should then read like:

```python
wf = workflow_from_ready("video/ltx2_3_lightricks_two_stage")

ltx_first_last_two_stage(
    wf,
    start_image_node="2004",
    end_image_node="47",
    stage1_condition_node="3159",
    stage2_condition_node="4970",
    stage2_sigmas=WAN2GP_LTX_STAGE2_SIGMAS,
)

register_reigh_video_inputs(wf)
```

Node IDs are still allowed internally because Comfy graphs are node graphs, but they are hidden behind named concepts.

**How Existing Pieces Fit**
- `ingest/normalize.py`
  Converts UI/API JSON into `VibeWorkflow`.

- `porting/workbench.py`
  Source-level doctor: custom nodes, model assets, schema issues, widget aliases.

- `porting/emitter.py`
  Emits pure Python from a `VibeWorkflow`.

- `registry/ready.py`
  Loads ready templates and detects source purity.

- `schema/validate.py`
  Low-level runtime shape validation.

- `patches/*`
  Reusable graph mutations.

- New `contracts/*`
  Semantic route/workflow assertions.

- New `lens/*` or expanded `analysis.graph`
  Named graph queries: upstream/downstream, edge source, node by registered input, stage chain discovery.

**Missing Pieces**
1. **Semantic graph lens**
   Helpers to ask:
   - what node owns `start_image`?
   - what consumes that image?
   - what sampler/stage does this conditioning feed?
   - what output node creates the artifact?

2. **Workflow contracts**
   Route-specific semantic requirements:
   - LTX first/last
   - LTX raw control video
   - LTX IC-LoRA pose/depth/canny/cameraman
   - Wan I2V
   - Wan VACE
   - animate/preprocess paths

3. **Contract CLI**
   A single command that gives pass/fail with useful diagnostics:
   ```bash
   vibecomfy workflow contract validate --all-app-routes
   ```

4. **Fork/apply helpers**
   Commands that generate clean derivative templates from official/community workflows:
   ```bash
   vibecomfy workflow fork video/ltx2_3_lightricks_two_stage \
     --pattern ltx-first-last-two-stage \
     --as video/ltx2_3_lightricks_first_last_parity
   ```

5. **Parity comparison runner**
   One command that runs Wan2GP and VibeComfy for the same route and records:
   - settings
   - model files
   - sampler/sigmas
   - inference time
   - wall time
   - VRAM
   - output file path
   - media sanity check

6. **Agent discoverability**
   Add to README/skill:
   “If you are adding/forking/onboarding a workflow, run `vibecomfy workflow port-check`, then `contract validate`, then RunPod parity.”

The key design principle: **the agent should not reason directly in raw Comfy node JSON unless debugging a low-level failure.** It should reason in contracts: first frame, last frame, control guide, LoRA chain, sampler, sigmas, dimensions, output artifact.

Goal\n+\n+VibeComfy should make it easy for an agent or developer to take any workflow source, whether official, community, forked, or built from scratch, and turn it into a pure-Python, app-ready Pieces\n+\n+VibeComfy already has most of the low-level machinery:\n+\n+- `vibecomfy.ingest.normalize`\n+  Converts UI/API workflow JSON into `VibeWorkflow`.\n+\n+- `vibecomfy.porting.workbench`\n+ It should not require compiled JSON except where runtime schema validation is explicitly needed.\n+\n+### 2. Workflow Contracts\n+\n+Add semantic contracts that describe what a route or workflow must do.\n+\n+Proposed module:\n+\n+```text\n+vibecomfy/contracts/\n+  base.py\n+  ltx.py\n+  wan.py\n+  reigh.py\n+```\n+\n+Contracts should validate:\n+\n+- required named inputs exist;\n+- named inputs reach the intended conditioning/control path;\n+- seeds are applied to all relevant samplers;\n+- dimensions and frame counts are bound to the actual latent/video path;\n+- LoRAs are chained into the actual model path;\n+- control inputs are routed to the expected guide/preprocessor;\n+- samplers, schedulers, sigmas, CFG, shift, and other parity-sensitive settings match the contract;\n+- output artifact nodes save to standard locations;\n+- model assets and custom nodes are declared;\n+- the template remains pure Python and does not load JSON at runtime.\n+\n+Example surface:\n+\n+```python\n+from vibecomfy.contracts.ltx import LTXFirstLastTwoStageContract\n+\n+contract = LTXFirstLastTwoStageContract(\n+    start_image=\"start_image\",\n+    end_image=\"end_image\",\n+    prompt=\"prompt\",\n+    negative=\"negative\",\n+    seed=(\"seed\", \"stage2_seed\"),\n+    dimensions=(\"width\", \"height\", \"frames\", \"fps\"),\n+    stage1_condition=\"first_frame\",\n+    stage2_condition=\"last_frame\",\n+    stage2_sigmas=\"0.909375, 0.725, 0.421875, 0.0\",\n+)\n+\n+contract.validate(workflow)\n+```\n+\n+Tests should use this layer instead of raw assertions like:\n+\n+```python\n+api[\"3336\"][\"inputs\"][\"image\"] == [\"4990\", 0]\n+```\n+\n+Compiled API checks should remain, but only as final runtime materialization checks.\n+\n+### 3. App Route Contracts\n+\n+Add route-level contracts for app integrations.\n+\n+For Reigh, each supported route should declare:\n+\n+- route key;\n+- template ID;\n+- required capability;\n+- required input patch points;\n+- expected workflow variation behavior;\n+- parity-sensitive settings;\n+- model and node-pack requirements;\n+- validation status;\n+- reference implementation, if any;\n+- RunPod validation evidence.\n+\n+Example:\n+\n+```yaml\n+route: travel_segment__model-ltx2_distilled__guidance-none__continuity-first_last__profile-default\n+template: video/ltx2_3_lightricks_first_last_parity\n+capability: first_last_frame_video\n+reference: wan2gp\n+contract:\n+  type: ltx_first_last_two_stage\n+  start_image: stage_1_condition\n+  end_image: stage_2_condition\n+  seed: stage_1_and_stage_2_noise\n+  dimensions: latent_canvas\n+  stage_2_sigmas: \"0.909375, 0.725, 0.421875, 0.0\"\n+validation:\n+  source_purity: required\n+  schema: required\n+  runpod_smoke: required\n+  parity_benchmark: required\n+```\n+\n+This should live in a machine-readable contract file, with docs generated from it if needed.\n+\n+### 4. Fork and Apply Helpers\n+\n+Add helpers for common workflow transformations so developers do not hand-edit node IDs for standard tasks.\n+\n+Examples:\n+\n+```bash\n+vibecomfy workflow fork video/ltx2_3_lightricks_two_stage \\\n+  --pattern ltx-first-last-two-stage \\\n+  --as video/ltx2_3_lightricks_first_last_parity\n+```\n+\n+This should:\n+\n+- load the base workflow;\n+- add or bind start/end image patch points;\n+- route stage 1 and stage 2 conditioning appropriately;\n+- set known parity constants;\n+- register named app inputs;\n+- preserve provenance;\n+- emit a pure Python manual template;\n+- generate or update semantic contract tests.\n+\n+Initial patterns worth supporting:\n+\n+- `ltx-first-last-two-stage`;\n+- `ltx-raw-video-guide`;\n+- `ltx-iclora-control`;\n+- `wan-i2v`;\n+- `wan-vace-first-last`;\n+- `wan-vace-video-source`;\n+- `animate-preprocess`;\n+- `image-edit-with-mask`.\n+\n+### 5. Contract CLI\n+\n+Add a single obvious command family for agents and developers.\n+\n+Suggested surface:\n+\n+```bash\n+vibecomfy workflow inspect <source-or-template>\n+vibecomfy workflow port-check <source-or-template>\n+vibecomfy workflow convert <source-json> --as video/foo\n+vibecomfy workflow lens <template>\n+vibecomfy workflow contract validate <template> --contract contracts/reigh/foo.yaml\n+vibecomfy workflow contract validate --all-ready\n+vibecomfy workflow parity run <route> --backend vibecomfy\n+vibecomfy workflow parity compare <route> --baseline wan2gp\n+```\n+\n+The existing commands can remain, but agents need one discoverable path for workflow work.\n+\n+Under the hood:\n+\n+- `workflow inspect` uses registry, lens, and source-info tools;\n+- `workflow port-check` delegates to `porting.workbench`;\n+- `workflow convert` delegates to the emitter/converter;\n+- `workflow contract validate` uses contracts plus source purity and schema validation;\n+- `workflow parity run/compare` can live in Reigh initially, but should produce VibeComfy-friendly reports.\n+\n+### 6. Parity Runner and Evidence Format\n+\n+Add a standard evidence format for app parity runs.\n+\n+Each run should capture:\n+\n+- route key;\n+- backend;\n+- template ID;\n+- git refs;\n+- RunPod pod ID, GPU type, data center, volume;\n+- input assets;\n+- model files actually loaded;\n+- custom node pack versions if available;\n+- prompt, negative prompt, dimensions, frames, FPS;\n+- seed;\n+- sampler, scheduler, CFG, sigmas, steps, shift;\n+- LoRAs and strengths;\n+- control mode and strength;\n+- warm/cold state;\n+- model download time;\n+- model load time where available;\n+- inference time;\n+- wall-clock time;\n+- peak VRAM/RAM where available;\n+- output artifact path;\n+- media sanity result;\n+- qualitative notes.\n+\n+Suggested artifact:\n+\n+```text\n+out/parity_runs/<timestamp>/<route>/\n+  report.json\n+  settings.json\n+  compiled_prompt.json\n+  source_contract.json\n+  logs/\n+  outputs/\n+```\n+\n+Comparison should separate:\n+\n+- end-to-end wall time;\n+- model/setup time;\n+- pure inference time;\n+- artifact transfer time.\n+\n+That distinction is necessary when comparing VibeComfy against Wan2GP.\n+\n+### 7.
